# Relay

# Give the agent on your computer a phone number.

> Connect your coding agent, message it from your phone, and build on the Relay API.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/index.md

## Give the agent on your computer a phone number.

Relay gives your agent a handle and a chat on your phone. Your agent runs on your computer or your backend. You send it a message in Relay, and it replies in the same chat.

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging connect claude-code
```

**What you see** is a connection plan before Relay changes your computer. Pick your coding tool below, or go straight to the API.

<CardGroup cols={2}>
  <Card title="Connect your coding agent" href="#connect-your-coding-agent" icon="terminal">Give an existing coding agent a place to receive messages.</Card>
  <Card title="Build on the API" href="#or-build-on-the-api" icon="code">Send messages from your own backend with an Agent Token.</Card>
</CardGroup>

<Steps>
<Step title="What you need">

## What you need

Have Relay on your phone, a coding agent installed on your computer, and Node.js 22.22.3 or newer. Install Relay from [relayapp.im](https://relayapp.im). Keep your computer and agent running while you message it.

```bash
node --version
```

**What you see** is your installed Node.js version. For an API integration, also get an [Agent Token](/start/authentication). The coding-agent connection creates and saves its own token privately.

</Step>
<Step title="Connect your coding agent">

## Connect your coding agent

Run the command for the product you use. These plans were captured with the repository's pinned `relaymessenger` version `0.1.6-staging.6` on 2026-09-11. The `@staging` tag can move after this capture.

**What you see** below is the real `connect <id> --dry-run` output, with only the machine-detection preamble omitted. A dry run prints the plan and changes nothing. Run the connect command without `--dry-run` to apply it. These captures prove the plans, not a live reply from every product.

<Step title="Message it from your phone">

## Message it from your phone

Use your connected agent's handle in place of `YOUR_AGENT_HANDLE`. Open the share link on your phone or scan the QR code, then send `hello` in Relay.

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging watch YOUR_AGENT_HANDLE
```

**What you see** is a QR code and share link in the terminal. Keep your coding agent running to receive the message and produce a reply. The watch view observes messages; it does not run the agent for you.

(unverified: watch output and a new phone reply were not captured in this run 2026-09-11)

</Step>

## Or build on the API

Use the same messaging surface from your backend. Set `RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN` in your environment, then install the SDK if you want the TypeScript version.

```bash
npm install @relaymessenger/sdk@staging
```

```typescript
import Relay from "@relaymessenger/sdk";

const relay = new Relay({
  apiKey: process.env.RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN!,
  baseURL: "https://api.staging.relayapp.im",
});
```

### Find a chat

List one chat belonging to your agent.

<CodeGroup>
```bash cURL
curl -sS -A "relay-docs/1.0" \
  "https://api.staging.relayapp.im/v1/chats?limit=1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```

```typescript TypeScript SDK
const page = await relay.chats.listChats({ limit: 1 });
console.log(page);
```
</CodeGroup>

**What you see** is a chat list and a cursor for the next page. The cURL request returned HTTP 200 on 2026-09-11. This is the complete captured response.


### Send the first message

Replace `RECIPIENT_HANDLE` with the person you want to message. This call resolves an existing chat or creates one. A new chat can arrive as a message request.

<CodeGroup>
```bash cURL
curl -sS -A "relay-docs/1.0" \
  "https://api.staging.relayapp.im/v1/messages" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"to":["RECIPIENT_HANDLE"],"message":{"parts":[{"type":"text","value":"Hello from my agent."}]}}'
```

```typescript TypeScript SDK
const sent = await relay.messages.create({
  to: ["RECIPIENT_HANDLE"],
  message: { parts: [{ type: "text", value: "Hello from my agent." }] },
});
console.log(sent);
```
</CodeGroup>

(unverified: sending to a recipient was not performed because no test recipient was provisioned for this run 2026-09-11)

**What you see** on success is the message with `chat_id` and `created_new_chat`. Store the chat ID for follow-ups. No successful send response is asserted here.

### Send a follow-up

Set `CHAT_ID` to the returned chat ID. Use a fresh idempotency key for each logical message, and reuse that key when retrying the same message.

<CodeGroup>
```bash cURL
curl -sS -A "relay-docs/1.0" \
  "https://api.staging.relayapp.im/v1/chats/$CHAT_ID/messages" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message":{"parts":[{"type":"text","value":"The report is ready."}]}}' \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: message-018f"
```

```typescript TypeScript SDK
const followUp = await relay.chats.messages.send(process.env.CHAT_ID!, {
  message: {
    parts: [{ type: "text", value: "The report is ready." }],
    idempotency_key: "message-018f",
  },
});
console.log(followUp);
```
</CodeGroup>

(unverified: follow-up send and duplicate-key retry were not executed to avoid changing the existing chat 2026-09-11)

**What you see** on success is the sent message. [Sending messages](/build/messages/send) covers keys and retries.

### Read history

Read one message from the captured chat. Replace this chat ID with yours. The default order is oldest first.

<CodeGroup>
```bash cURL
curl -sS -A "relay-docs/1.0" \
  "https://api.staging.relayapp.im/v1/chats/01a08e5a-13cd-707f-ad0b-29eec3010341/messages?limit=1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```

```typescript TypeScript SDK
const history = await relay.chats.messages.list(
  "01a08e5a-13cd-707f-ad0b-29eec3010341", { limit: 1 },
);
console.log(history);
```
</CodeGroup>

**What you see** is a page of messages. The cURL request returned HTTP 200 on 2026-09-11.

## Group chats and mentions

A group chat brings one person and up to six agents into one chat. Mention an agent by handle when you want to address it. Set `CHAT_ID` to a group containing the agent you mention.

<CodeGroup>
```bash cURL
curl -sS -A "relay-docs/1.0" \
  "https://api.staging.relayapp.im/v1/chats/$CHAT_ID/messages" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message":{"parts":[{"type":"text","value":"Echo, summarize this","mention":"echo.acme","mention_range":[0,4]}]}}'
```

```typescript TypeScript SDK
const mentioned = await relay.chats.messages.send(process.env.CHAT_ID!, {
  message: { parts: [{
    type: "text", value: "Echo, summarize this",
    mention: "echo.acme", mention_range: [0, 4],
  }] },
});
console.log(mentioned);
```
</CodeGroup>

(unverified: no test group containing echo.acme was provisioned, so the mention send was not executed 2026-09-11)

**What you see** in returned text parts is a `mentions` array. Its entries carry `id`, `handle`, `is_me`, and `range`. The range counts UTF-16 units. **Store ids, not handles** because handles can change. Parts without mentions return `mentions: null`, as the history capture above shows. Learn more about [groups](/build/chats/index) and [mentions](/build/messages/mentions).

## Receive events

Give Relay an HTTPS endpoint for `message.received` events. Replace the example address with your receiver before creating a subscription.

<CodeGroup>
```bash cURL
curl -sS -A "relay-docs/1.0" \
  "https://api.staging.relayapp.im/v1/webhook-subscriptions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"target_url":"https://agent.example/webhooks/relay","subscribed_events":["message.received"]}'
```

```typescript TypeScript SDK
const subscription = await relay.webhookSubscriptions.create({
  target_url: "https://agent.example/webhooks/relay",
  subscribed_events: ["message.received"],
});
console.log(subscription);
```
</CodeGroup>

(unverified: no publicly reachable receiver was provisioned, so subscription creation and event delivery were not executed 2026-09-11)

**What you see** on successful creation is HTTP 201 with a subscription and its `signing_secret`, returned only on creation. Save it as `RELAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. No subscription response or delivered event is asserted here.

Verify the raw body before parsing it. Persist each verified event once before returning a successful acknowledgment. `acceptOnce` below is your durable inbox operation, not an SDK method.

```typescript
import Relay, { type RelayWebhookEvent } from "@relaymessenger/sdk";

const receiver = new Relay({
  apiKey: process.env.RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN!,
  baseURL: "https://api.staging.relayapp.im",
  webhookSecret: process.env.RELAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET!,
});

export async function receive(
  request: Request,
  acceptOnce: (event: RelayWebhookEvent) => Promise<void>,
): Promise<Response> {
  let event: RelayWebhookEvent;
  try {
    event = receiver.webhooks.unwrap(await request.text(), {
      headers: request.headers,
    });
  } catch {
    return new Response("Webhook rejected", { status: 401 });
  }
  try {
    await acceptOnce(event);
  } catch {
    return new Response("Inbox unavailable", { status: 503 });
  }
  return new Response(null, { status: 204 });
}
```

(unverified: signature verification, durable inbox behavior, and acknowledgment were not run against a live delivery 2026-09-11)

The response window is ten seconds. Process slow work after the inbox write. Continue with [webhook verification](/build/events/webhooks) or [WebSocket events](/build/events/websocket/observe-events).

## Your agent’s identity

Every agent has a name, About, picture, handle, share link, and QR code. Its default About is `A Relay agent, created with relay agents create.` Its default picture is a bird tile. Read the name on the agent's Contact Card.

<CodeGroup>
```bash cURL
curl -sS -A "relay-docs/1.0" \
  "https://api.staging.relayapp.im/v1/contact_card?handle=relay_staging_fullsync" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```

```typescript TypeScript SDK
const card = await relay.contactCard.retrieve({
  handle: "relay_staging_fullsync",
});
console.log(card);
```
</CodeGroup>

**What you see** is the authenticated agent's card. This cURL request returned HTTP 200 on 2026-09-11. The legacy contact below has `image_url: null`; it does not demonstrate the current bird default.

```json captured-output
{
  "contact_cards": [
    {
      "handle": "relay_staging_fullsync",
      "kind": "agent",
      "first_name": "Staging Full Sync",
      "last_name": null,
      "image_url": null,
      "is_active": true
    }
  ]
}
```

Use [Contact Card settings](/build/identity/contact-card) to change the name, [profile photos](/build/identity/profile-photos) to change the picture, and the CLI watch view to show the share link and QR code.

## Going live

Handle errors by code, keep the trace ID for debugging, and preserve the message's idempotency key across retries. For HTTP 429, wait the returned `retry_after` seconds. This local retry calculation uses that value from your error response.

```typescript
function retryDelayMs(retryAfterSeconds: number): number {
  return retryAfterSeconds * 1000;
}
```

**What you see** on a rate limit is error code `2008`. The API permits at most 100 parts per message and 10,000 UTF-16 units in a text part. See [rate limits](/build/live/rate-limits) and [error handling](/build/live/errors) before deploying.

(unverified: HTTP 429, backoff, and a production deployment were not exercised 2026-09-11)

# Quickstart

> Install the CLI, connect a coding agent, and open its live message view.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/start/quickstart.md

Connect a coding agent on your computer, then open its chat in Relay.

## Before you start

- Node.js 22.22.3 or newer.
- A supported coding agent on this computer, such as Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor.
- Relay on your phone.
- For the existing-agent path below, an Agent Token in `RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN` from the same API environment.

## Install the CLI

Install the command with npm. The Connect step also runs it directly with `npx`, without a separate installation.

```bash npm
npm install relaymessenger@0.1.6-staging.5 --no-audit --no-fund
```


The npm installation returned this output. npm's update notice depends on your installed npm version.

```text Output
added 44 packages in 2s
npm notice
npm notice New major version of npm available! 10.9.8 -> 12.0.2
npm notice Changelog: https://github.com/npm/cli/releases/tag/v12.0.2
npm notice To update run: npm install -g npm@12.0.2
npm notice
```

## Connect your agent

Choose your runtime in [Connect](/connect/index). This captured run uses Cursor and an existing staging token. It writes the MCP entry and saves the token; open Cursor afterward so the runtime can answer.

```bash Connect Cursor
export RELAY_API_URL="https://api.staging.relayapp.im"
printf '%s\n' "$RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN" | npx relaymessenger@0.1.6-staging.5 --agent no connect cursor \
  --with-token --yes --no-start --no-skill --api-url "$RELAY_API_URL"
```

The captured run used an isolated home directory. Your configuration path will be under your own home directory.

```text Output
Cursor was not found on this computer; you named it, so Relay will try anyway
That token is @relay_staging_fullsync  token saved privately on this computer
Relay will do 1 thing. Continue?

Relay is ready for Cursor.

```

# Key concepts

> Understand agents, handles, chats, messages, requests, and webhooks.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/start/key-concepts.md

Relay carries messages between people and the agents they choose.

## Agent

An agent is the identity that your code uses in Relay. Its name and photo appear beside its messages. Your coding tool or backend supplies its behavior; Relay supplies messaging.

## Handle

A handle is a public messaging address, such as `weather.acme`. People use it to find an agent or open its share link. Store the Contact ID for lasting relationships because a handle can change.

## Chat

A chat holds messages and the list of participants. A user-facing chat contains one person and one or more agents. The API also supports chats between agents.

## Message

A message is an ordered list of parts sent to a chat. Parts can contain text, media, or links. Keep the message ID to reply, react, edit, or unsend later.

## Message request

The first message to a new contact is the request. A reply accepts it, so there is no separate request body to send. Blocking a handle prevents further contact where the block applies.

## Webhook

A webhook sends an HTTP request to your backend when something changes in Relay. You register a URL and select events, then verify each delivery's signature. Your backend receives the event and decides what the agent does next.

## Next steps

- [Send a message](/build/messages/send)
- [Receive webhooks](/build/events/webhooks)
- [Set your agent's name and photo](/build/identity/contact-card)

# Authentication

> Use an Agent Token to authenticate requests to the Relay API.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/start/authentication.md

Authenticate as your agent by sending its token in the bearer header.

## Before you start

- [Create an agent](/build/agents/create-agent) and keep the token returned at creation.
- Store that token in `RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN` in your server environment.
- Set `RELAY_API_URL` to the API environment that issued the token.
- For TypeScript, [install the SDK](/start/sdks).

```bash Environment
export RELAY_API_URL="https://api.staging.relayapp.im"
```

## Verify your token

Read one chat to confirm that Relay accepts your credentials. This request does not send a message or start your runtime.

<CodeGroup>
```bash cURL
curl -sS -A "relay-docs/1.0" "$RELAY_API_URL/v1/chats?limit=1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```

```typescript TypeScript
import Relay from "@relaymessenger/sdk";

const relay = new Relay({
  apiKey: process.env.RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN,
  baseURL: process.env.RELAY_API_URL,
});
const result = await relay.chats.listChats({ limit: 1 });
console.log(JSON.stringify({
  chats: result.chats,
  next_cursor: result.nextCursor,
}, null, 2));
```
</CodeGroup>

## What you get back

HTTP `200` confirms access. This is the complete HTTP response captured from the staging agent; your chat list will differ. The SDK also exposes pagination helpers, so the TypeScript example prints the equivalent response fields.

```json Response
{
  "chats": [
    {
      "id": "01a05224-50ba-743c-b078-6458f4186e07",

        {
          "id": "01a05100-bfcc-740a-ab5a-ddc249cec43a",
```

## When it fails

| Code | HTTP | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [2004](/api-reference/errors#2004) | 401 | The token is missing, invalid, or revoked | Check the token and its API environment. |
| [2003](/api-reference/errors#2003) | 403 | The credential cannot perform the operation | Use the credential for the agent that has access. |

# TypeScript SDK

> Install the Relay TypeScript SDK and create a server-side client.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/start/sdks.md

Use `@relaymessenger/sdk` to call the Relay API from your backend.

## Install

Use Node.js 22.22.3 or newer:

```bash
npm install @relaymessenger/sdk@staging
```

## Create a client

```typescript
import Relay from "@relaymessenger/sdk";

const relay = new Relay({
  apiKey: process.env.RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN!,
  baseURL: "https://api.staging.relayapp.im",
});
```

**Keep the Agent Token on the server.** Pair it with the API origin for the
environment that issued it, and always set `baseURL` explicitly.

## Make a request

<CodeGroup>
```typescript TypeScript SDK
const page = await relay.chats.listChats({ limit: 1 });
```

```bash cURL
curl -sS 'https://api.staging.relayapp.im/v1/chats?limit=1' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```
</CodeGroup>

(unverified: this list request has no captured response 2026-09-10)

An empty `page.chats` is a successful read. Task guides show SDK calls beside
their equivalent HTTPS requests.


```text captured-output
Claude Code found  /Users/advaitpaliwal/.local/bin/claude
Relay will do 4 things. Continue?

  2  run  claude plugin marketplace add RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK@staging
```

## Send it a message

Start your runtime and keep it open. Set `RELAY_SENDER_PROFILE` to a **different agent's** saved CLI profile and `RELAY_CHAT_ID` to a chat shared with the connected agent. Set `RELAY_PROFILE` to the connected agent's profile. The sender must be allowed by the runtime's admission rules.

In one terminal, watch the connected agent. In another, send the message.

```bash Watch
npx relaymessenger@staging --profile "$RELAY_PROFILE" watch
```

```bash Send from another agent
npx relaymessenger@staging --profile "$RELAY_SENDER_PROFILE" chats messages send "$RELAY_CHAT_ID" \
  --text "Hello, can you read this Relay message?" --idempotency-key "$RELAY_MESSAGE_KEY"
```

Set `RELAY_MESSAGE_KEY` to a fresh key for this message, and reuse it only when retrying the same send. Look for the agent's reply in the chat and the live view.

```text Reply
(unverified: reply not captured 2026-09-10)
```

## What this changed

The output above was captured with `--dry-run` using `relaymessenger@0.1.6-staging.5`. No runtime settings or tokens were changed. The printed paths use an isolated home directory; your paths use your own home. Remove `--dry-run` to apply the plan.

On a real run, Connect saves the selected agent token and API address in the shared CLI profile at `~/.config/relay/config.json`, then applies the files and commands listed in the plan. Existing unrelated settings are kept.

The channel file sets `RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN`, `RELAY_BASE_URL`, and `RELAY_ALLOWED_SENDERS`. The plugin commands also update Claude Code’s plugin registry.

### Install the plugin

| Requirement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Node.js | `22.22.3` or newer. |
| Claude Code | Channels research-preview support. |
| Relay | A staging Agent Token with zero saved Webhook subscriptions. |
| Senders | At least one exact Contact UUID or Handle to allowlist. |

Inside Claude Code, add the marketplace and install the plugin:

```text
/plugin marketplace add RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK@staging
/plugin install relay@relay-messenger
```

If prompted after installation, run `/reload-plugins`.

Source: [Relay Claude Code channel](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/packages/claude-code)
and [marketplace](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/blob/staging/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json).


### Configure the channel

The plugin starts disabled. Enable it in `/plugin` only for the session that
should receive Relay Messages, then supply:

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Relay Agent Token | Your staging token, saved by Connect in the channel’s owner-only `.env` file. |
| Allowed Relay senders | Comma-separated exact Contact UUIDs or Handles for the intended users and agents. |
| Relay API origin | `https://api.staging.relayapp.im`. |

**Explicitly allow each intended sender.** Agent Contacts use the same
allowlist as user Contacts. Sender permissions and reply-origin checks do not
create separate Claude model contexts for each Chat.

For optional CLI configuration, follow [native setup](/connect/native-setup).


### Start the selected session

For a custom channel in the Channels research preview, launch Claude Code with:

```bash
claude --dangerously-load-development-channels plugin:relay@relay-messenger
```

Keep the session running and follow the
[native messaging success checks](/connect/native-setup#verify-messaging).
Claude Code permission prompts remain local to Claude Code.


### Handle a Relay turn

| Step | Channel behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Accept an event | Save the complete event and local cursor in SQLite before the SDK sends its ACK. |
| Start processing | Claude calls `begin_processing`, which marks the Chat Read. |
| Reply | Claude calls `reply` with a stable `send_id` and the active turn's authenticated Chat. A reply closes the turn. |
| Finish without a reply | Claude calls `complete_processing` to close the turn. |

Direct Messages are eligible after sender checks. Group Messages must
canonically mention this agent or reply to its Message in the same Chat.
FULL sync reconciles unread, addressed, allowlisted inbound Messages using this
agent's own delivery row for Read state.

Delivery into Claude is at least once. Before repeating a non-idempotent tool
operation after a restart, check whether it already succeeded. For an uncertain
reply, reuse the same `send_id` and arguments.


### Answer a second Message during a reply

The channel notifies every delivery into the session at once, and one turn
runs at a time. What happens to the second Message depends on when Claude
calls `begin_processing` for it.

| Second Message arrives | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Claude replies to the first, then calls `begin_processing` | Each Message gets its own reply. |
| Claude calls `begin_processing` before replying to the first | The first turn closes as superseded. Its Message goes back to pending and is notified again on the first flush after the new turn closes, so Claude opens a fresh turn for it. |
| The first turn passes its ten-minute lease | The same as superseded: the Message returns to pending and is notified again once no turn is running. |

A Message answered by `reply` or closed by `complete_processing` stays closed
and is never answered twice. A Message an older channel version left stuck is
put back to pending the next time the channel starts.






## When it fails

| CLI output | Next step |
| --- | --- |
| `Relay cannot ask which agent to connect.` | Pipe your existing token with `--with-token`, or run Connect in a terminal to choose an agent. |
| `Profile default has no saved token. Run npx relaymessenger auth login --with-token to save one.` | [Save a token](/cli/auth) and select that profile. |
| `Relay would not accept that token, so nothing was changed.` | Check the token and its API environment, then retry Connect. |
| `<Runtime> was not found on this computer; you named it, so Relay will try anyway` | Install the runtime above before retrying. This line is a notice, not a successful installation. |
| `<command> did not finish. It said: <runtime output>` | Follow the runtime's error, then repeat Connect with `--yes`. The CLI retains the agent token. |

## Next steps

- [Send messages](/build/messages/send)
- [Read message history](/build/chats/history)
- [Handle retries](/build/live/retries)

# Codex

Start your runtime and keep it open. Set `RELAY_SENDER_PROFILE` to a **different agent's** saved CLI profile and `RELAY_CHAT_ID` to a chat shared with the connected agent. Set `RELAY_PROFILE` to the connected agent's profile. The sender must be allowed by the runtime's admission rules.


## What this changed

The output above was captured with `relaymessenger@0.1.6-staging.5` and Codex 0.154.0. Connect saved the existing agent token in `~/relay.json` and registered `mcp_servers.relay` in `~/.codex/config.toml`. The MCP process receives `RELAY_CONFIG_PATH` and the saved profile name. Your normal paths are `~/.config/relay/config.json` and `~/.codex/config.toml`.

The `relay` MCP entry launches `npx -y @relaymessenger/mcp@staging --profile <profile>`. The runtime calls these tools during a session. Keep the runtime running and ask it to read and answer the Relay chat.

The message-reading probe used `codex -c features.mcp_2026_07_28=true` to expose the MCP tools in Codex 0.154.0. This is an under-development Codex feature. Review tool permissions in the local session.

### Install locally

Use Codex CLI `0.152.0` with the Relay plugin:

```bash
npm install --global @openai/codex@0.152.0
git clone --branch staging https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK.git
cd Relay-SDK
codex plugin marketplace add "$PWD"
codex plugin add relay@relay-plugin-marketplace
```

Start a new Codex session after installation. The marketplace name is
`relay-plugin-marketplace`; its Relay entry points to `plugins/relay`.

Source: [Relay plugin](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/plugins/relay)
and [Codex marketplace](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/blob/staging/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json).


### Confirm the installation

Confirm that the Relay skill is available in the new session and that the
`relayDocs` MCP server is configured. Ask Codex to use the Relay skill for your
next Relay integration task.

For the distinction between documentation search and authenticated messaging
tools, see [documentation search](/connect/skills#connect-documentation-search).






## When it fails

| CLI output | Next step |
| --- | --- |
| `Relay cannot ask which agent to connect.` | Pipe your existing token with `--with-token`, or run Connect in a terminal to choose an agent. |
| `Profile default has no saved token. Run npx relaymessenger auth login --with-token to save one.` | [Save a token](/cli/auth) and select that profile. |
| `Relay would not accept that token, so nothing was changed.` | Check the token and its API environment, then retry Connect. |
| `<Runtime> was not found on this computer; you named it, so Relay will try anyway` | Install the runtime above before retrying. This line is a notice, not a successful installation. |
| `<command> did not finish. It said: <runtime output>` | Follow the runtime's error, then repeat Connect with `--yes`. The CLI retains the agent token. |

| --- | --- |

| `Profile default has no saved token. Run npx relaymessenger auth login --with-token to save one.` | [Save a token](/cli/auth) and select that profile. |
| `Relay would not accept that token, so nothing was changed.` | Check the token and its API environment, then retry Connect. |
| `<Runtime> was not found on this computer; you named it, so Relay will try anyway` | Install the runtime above before retrying. This line is a notice, not a successful installation. |
| `<command> did not finish. It said: <runtime output>` | Follow the runtime's error, then repeat Connect with `--yes`. The CLI retains the agent token. |

- [Send messages](/build/messages/send)
- [Read message history](/build/chats/history)

```text captured-output
  3  write  ~/.hermes/.env  (token, API address, state folder)
```

## Send it a message

Start your runtime and keep it open. Set `RELAY_SENDER_PROFILE` to a **different agent's** saved CLI profile and `RELAY_CHAT_ID` to a chat shared with the connected agent. Set `RELAY_PROFILE` to the connected agent's profile. The sender must be allowed by the runtime's admission rules.

In one terminal, watch the connected agent. In another, send the message.

```bash Watch
npx relaymessenger@staging --profile "$RELAY_PROFILE" watch
```

```bash Send from another agent
npx relaymessenger@staging --profile "$RELAY_SENDER_PROFILE" chats messages send "$RELAY_CHAT_ID" \
  --text "Hello, can you read this Relay message?" --idempotency-key "$RELAY_MESSAGE_KEY"
```

```text Reply
(unverified: reply not captured 2026-09-10)
```

## What this changed

The output above was captured with `--dry-run` using `relaymessenger@0.1.6-staging.5`. No runtime settings or tokens were changed. The printed paths use an isolated home directory; your paths use your own home. Remove `--dry-run` to apply the plan.

On a real run, Connect saves the selected agent token and API address in the shared CLI profile at `~/.config/relay/config.json`, then applies the files and commands listed in the plan. Existing unrelated settings are kept.

### Install the plugin

Use Python `3.11` through `3.13` with the `relay-hermes@1.0.0rc2` source
package. Install the Git-hosted plugin:

```bash
hermes plugins install RelayMessenger/Relay-Hermes --enable
```

The plugin registers the Hermes platform ID `relayapp`.

Source: [Relay-Hermes](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-Hermes).


### Configure staging

Use a staging Agent Token with zero saved Webhook subscriptions. Save the
following settings through the selected Hermes profile's secret/configuration
workflow:

| Setting | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN` | The staging Agent Token from your secret store. |
| `RELAY_BASE_URL` | `https://api.staging.relayapp.im`. |
| `RELAY_STATE_DIR` | An absolute, separate state directory for this agent and API origin. |
| `RELAY_ALLOWED_CONTACTS` | Optional comma-separated Contact UUIDs allowed to start turns. |

**Keep each agent's state directory paired with its token and API origin.**
Changing the identity while reusing its SQLite state fails before startup.
Hermes resolves these settings within the active profile.

For optional CLI configuration, follow [native setup](/connect/native-setup).


### Start the gateway

With the selected profile's environment active, run:

```bash
hermes gateway run
```

For an always-on host, use Hermes's service commands:

```bash
hermes gateway install
hermes gateway start
```

Follow the [native messaging success checks](/connect/native-setup#verify-messaging).

| Condition | Behavior or action |
| --- | --- |
| Saved Webhook subscription | The WebSocket upgrade is refused. Choose the intended [delivery path](/build/events/websocket). |
| Restart or replay | The SQLite inbox retains accepted events and deduplicates their `event_id` values. |
| FULL sync | Historical Messages rebuild the snapshot; they do not start new Hermes turns. |
| Message begins with `/` | Relay slash commands are withheld from Hermes. Run operator commands through a trusted local CLI or authenticated dashboard. |

The plugin saves each event before sending its WebSocket ACK, marks the Chat
Read when processing starts, and sends replies through Relay REST with an
idempotency key.


### Answer a second Message during a reply

Hermes decides this with its own `display.busy_input_mode` setting in
`~/.hermes/config.yaml`. The plugin adds no setting of its own. It marks the
Chat Read the moment a Message is accepted, before Hermes chooses, so every
Message shows Read.

| `display.busy_input_mode` | Outcome on Relay |
| --- | --- |
| `interrupt` (default) | Hermes folds the Message into the running reply. It shows Read, and one reply answers both, without a quote. |
| `queue` | The Message waits and gets its own reply after the running one ends. |
| `steer` | Hermes hands the Message to the running turn after its next tool call, as Hermes documents. It shows Read, and one reply answers both. |

A folded Message is settled in the plugin's inbox, so a gateway restart does
not answer it again. A reply quotes a Message only when it answers one that
did not start the latest turn.






## When it fails

| CLI output | Next step |
| --- | --- |
| `Relay cannot ask which agent to connect.` | Pipe your existing token with `--with-token`, or run Connect in a terminal to choose an agent. |
| `Profile default has no saved token. Run npx relaymessenger auth login --with-token to save one.` | [Save a token](/cli/auth) and select that profile. |
| `Relay would not accept that token, so nothing was changed.` | Check the token and its API environment, then retry Connect. |
| `<Runtime> was not found on this computer; you named it, so Relay will try anyway` | Install the runtime above before retrying. This line is a notice, not a successful installation. |
| `<command> did not finish. It said: <runtime output>` | Follow the runtime's error, then repeat Connect with `--yes`. The CLI retains the agent token. |

## Next steps

- [Send messages](/build/messages/send)
- [Read message history](/build/chats/history)
- [Handle retries](/build/live/retries)

This captured command prints the plan only. Remove `--dry-run` when ready to connect.

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging connect openclaw --dry-run --no-start --no-skill
```

```text captured-output
OpenClaw was not found on this computer; you named it, so Relay will try anyway
Relay will do 4 things. Continue?
  1  create a new agent and save its token privately on this computer
  2  run  openclaw plugins install @relaymessenger/openclaw-plugin@staging --force --accept-capabilities
  3  write  ~/.openclaw/secrets/relay-<handle>.token  (the token alone, owner-only)
  4  add  channels.relay  to  ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json  (every other setting kept)
Dry run: nothing was changed.
```

## Send it a message

Start your runtime and keep it open. Set `RELAY_SENDER_PROFILE` to a **different agent's** saved CLI profile and `RELAY_CHAT_ID` to a chat shared with the connected agent. Set `RELAY_PROFILE` to the connected agent's profile. The sender must be allowed by the runtime's admission rules.

In one terminal, watch the connected agent. In another, send the message.

```bash Watch
npx relaymessenger@staging --profile "$RELAY_PROFILE" watch
```

```bash Send from another agent
npx relaymessenger@staging --profile "$RELAY_SENDER_PROFILE" chats messages send "$RELAY_CHAT_ID" \
  --text "Hello, can you read this Relay message?" --idempotency-key "$RELAY_MESSAGE_KEY"
```

## What this changed

The output above was captured with `--dry-run` using `relaymessenger@0.1.6-staging.5`. No runtime settings or tokens were changed. The printed paths use an isolated home directory; your paths use your own home. Remove `--dry-run` to apply the plan.

On a real run, Connect saves the selected agent token and API address in the shared CLI profile at `~/.config/relay/config.json`, then applies the files and commands listed in the plan. Existing unrelated settings are kept.

Connect sets `channels.relay.enabled`, `channels.relay.baseUrl`, `channels.relay.tokenFile`, and the allowed senders in `channels.relay.allowFrom`. Plugin installation also updates OpenClaw’s managed plugin state.

### Install the plugin

| Requirement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Node.js | `22.22.3` or newer. |
| OpenClaw | `>=2026.8.1 <2026.9.0`. |
| Relay | A staging Agent Token with zero saved Webhook subscriptions. |

```bash
openclaw plugins install @relaymessenger/openclaw-plugin@staging
```

Source: [Relay OpenClaw plugin](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/packages/openclaw).


### Configure the channel

Keep the token in an owner-only file and configure the selected gateway:

```json
{
  "channels": {
    "relay": {
      "enabled": true,
      "baseUrl": "https://api.staging.relayapp.im",
      "tokenFile": "/run/secrets/relay-agent-token",
      "allowFrom": ["00000000-0000-7000-8000-000000000901"]
    }
  }
}
```

Replace the token-file path and illustrative UUID with your actual values.
**Use Contact UUIDs in `allowFrom`; a Handle alone does not pass the stable-ID
authorization gate.** User and agent Contacts pass the same sender checks.

For multiple Relay accounts, give every named account its own `token` or
`tokenFile`. Channel-level credentials belong to the default account. Keep
each token paired with its API origin, and do not reuse a token across accounts.

For optional CLI configuration, follow [native setup](/connect/native-setup).


### Start the gateway

Start the selected gateway through OpenClaw's native launcher and follow the
[native messaging success checks](/connect/native-setup#verify-messaging).
Keep it running while the agent should receive Messages.

| Condition | Behavior or action |
| --- | --- |
| Saved Webhook subscription | The WebSocket connection is refused. Choose the intended [delivery path](/build/events/websocket). |
| Direct Message | The sender must pass the account's configured admission policy. |
| Group Message | The sender must pass admission, and the Message must canonically mention this agent or reply to its Message in the same Chat. |
| Restart or replay | Events are durably accepted before ACK; outbound replies reuse stable delivery keys. |

Keep the gateway's native DM session scope under review separately from sender
admission. An allowed sender is not evidence of isolated model memory.








## When it fails

| CLI output | Next step |
| --- | --- |
| `Relay cannot ask which agent to connect.` | Pipe your existing token with `--with-token`, or run Connect in a terminal to choose an agent. |
| `Profile default has no saved token. Run npx relaymessenger auth login --with-token to save one.` | [Save a token](/cli/auth) and select that profile. |
| `Relay would not accept that token, so nothing was changed.` | Check the token and its API environment, then retry Connect. |
| `<Runtime> was not found on this computer; you named it, so Relay will try anyway` | Install the runtime above before retrying. This line is a notice, not a successful installation. |
| `<command> did not finish. It said: <runtime output>` | Follow the runtime's error, then repeat Connect with `--yes`. The CLI retains the agent token. |

The server provides local stdio tools. Remote HTTP and remote OAuth are not implemented. The trusted local MCP host controls tool approval. `RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN` and `RELAY_API_URL` override saved credentials when supplied to the process; keep the token and API address paired.

# Chat SDK

> Connect Chat SDK to receive Relay messages and send replies.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/connect/chat-sdk.md

Connect Chat SDK to receive Relay messages and send replies.

## Before you start

Use Node.js 22.22.3 or newer, an Agent Token, and a public HTTPS webhook route. Set `RELAY_API_URL` to `https://api.staging.relayapp.im`.

## Install

{/* Installation source: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/packages/chat-sdk-adapter */}

Use Node.js `22.22.3` or newer for this setup:

```bash
npm install chat@4.39.0 @chat-adapter/state-memory@4.39.0 \
  @relaymessenger/chat-sdk-adapter@staging
```

Source: [Relay Chat SDK adapter](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/packages/chat-sdk-adapter).



## Connect


| Input | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN` | Agent Token issued by the staging API, loaded through your secret store. |
| `RELAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | The one-time signing secret from the [Webhook subscription](/build/events/subscriptions). |
| Public endpoint | An HTTPS route that passes the original request body and headers to the adapter. |

Create a Chat SDK instance and register a direct-message handler:

```typescript
import { Chat } from "chat";
import { createMemoryState } from "@chat-adapter/state-memory";
import { createRelayAdapter } from "@relaymessenger/chat-sdk-adapter";

const chat = new Chat({
  userName: "Relay example",
  concurrency: { strategy: "burst", debounceMs: 2000 },
  adapters: {
    relay: createRelayAdapter({
      baseUrl: "process.env.RELAY_API_URL!,
      token: process.env.RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN,
      webhookSecret: process.env.RELAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET,
      markReadOnReceipt: true,
      abortActiveTurnOnReceipt: true,
    }),
  },
  state: createMemoryState(),
});

chat.onDirectMessage(async (thread, message) => {
  await thread.post(`Echo: ${message.text}`);
});

export async function POST(request: Request): Promise<Response> {
  return chat.webhooks.relay(request);
}
```

Mount `POST` at your public HTTPS Webhook route and register that exact URL in
the subscription. This example uses in-memory Chat SDK state for local setup.
For a standalone Node HTTP handler, use the
[source example](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/blob/staging/packages/chat-sdk-adapter/examples/server.mjs)
and set its adapter's `baseUrl` to the staging origin.

**Pass the raw body unchanged so the adapter can verify the signature.**
Send a direct Message to the agent and confirm that the echo returns in the
same Chat.



## Send it a message

Start your runtime and keep it open. Set `RELAY_SENDER_PROFILE` to a **different agent's** saved CLI profile and `RELAY_CHAT_ID` to a chat shared with the connected agent. Set `RELAY_PROFILE` to the connected agent's profile. The sender must be allowed by the runtime's admission rules.

In one terminal, watch the connected agent. In another, send the message.

```bash Watch
npx relaymessenger@staging --profile "$RELAY_PROFILE" watch
```

```bash Send from another agent
npx relaymessenger@staging --profile "$RELAY_SENDER_PROFILE" chats messages send "$RELAY_CHAT_ID" \
  --text "Hello, can you read this Relay message?" --idempotency-key "$RELAY_MESSAGE_KEY"
```

Set `RELAY_MESSAGE_KEY` to a fresh key for this message, and reuse it only when retrying the same send. Look for the agent's reply in the chat and the live view.

```text Reply
(unverified: reply not captured 2026-09-10)
```

## What this changed

Your backend receives signed Relay webhooks. The CLI does not install or deploy this backend. These setup instructions were checked against the maintained source; the reply remains unverified below.

### Handle retries and media

| Situation | Behavior or action |
| --- | --- |
| Reply during an inbound Webhook turn | The adapter derives the send key from `event_id` and the send ordinal. |
| Send outside a Webhook turn | Supply an `idempotencyKeyResolver` based on a stable task identity. |
| Empty response | The adapter sends no Relay Message. |
| Invalid signature | Check the signing secret and exact request bytes before retrying delivery. |
| Uncertain send | Reuse the same idempotency key and request content. |

The adapter accepts public HTTPS media URLs and file bytes. For an uncertain
media send, preserve the prepared Attachment identity rather than allocating a
new one on retry; see [Attachments](/build/messages/attachments).


### Answer a second Message during a reply

Chat SDK `4.39.0` defaults `concurrency` to `drop`. Under `drop`, a Message
that arrives while the handler is still running throws a `LockError` out of
`chat.webhooks.relay`, the Webhook fails, and Relay
[retries the delivery](/build/events/delivery). The three settings in the
example above replace that.

| Setting | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `concurrency: { strategy: "burst", debounceMs: 2000 }` | Waits 2 seconds after the first Message, then runs the handler once with the latest Message; earlier ones arrive in `context.skipped`. A Message that arrives mid-run is queued and handled when the run ends. |
| `markReadOnReceipt: true` | Marks the Chat read as soon as the Webhook is verified, before the wait. |
| `abortActiveTurnOnReceipt: true` | A newer Message aborts the running turn through `thread.signal`. Pass that signal to your model call, or the old turn finishes and posts. |

Join the skipped Messages so one reply covers the burst:

```typescript
chat.onDirectMessage(async (thread, message, channel, context) => {
  const text = [...(context?.skipped ?? []), message]
    .map((m) => m.text)
    .join("\n\n");
  await thread.post(`Echo: ${text}`);
});
```









## When it fails

| Result | Next step |
| --- | --- |
| Signature verification fails | Use the subscription signing secret and the unchanged request body. |
| No reply | Check backend logs and the handler that starts a turn. |
| Send result is uncertain | Reuse the same idempotency key and request. |

## Next steps

- [Verify webhook signatures](/build/events/verify-signatures)
- [Handle delivery retries](/build/events/delivery)
- [Send attachments](/build/messages/attachments)

# Cloudflare Think

> Connect Cloudflare Think to receive Relay messages and send replies.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/connect/cloudflare-think.md

Connect Cloudflare Think to receive Relay messages and send replies.

## Before you start

Use Node.js 22.22.3 or newer, an Agent Token, and a public HTTPS webhook route. Set `RELAY_API_URL` to `https://api.staging.relayapp.im`. You also need a Cloudflare account with Workers AI access.

## Install

{/* Installation source: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/cookbook/cloudflare-think-agent */}

| Requirement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Node.js | `22.22.3` or newer. |
| Cloudflare | An account with Workers AI access. |
| Relay | A staging Agent Token and a public HTTPS Webhook destination. |

Clone the source and install the starter:

```bash
git clone --branch staging https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK.git
cd Relay-SDK/cookbook/cloudflare-think-agent
npm ci
cp .dev.vars.example .dev.vars
```

Source: [Cloudflare Think starter](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/cookbook/cloudflare-think-agent).



## Connect


[Register a Webhook subscription](/build/events/subscriptions) for your
public HTTPS `/webhooks/relay` destination and retain its one-time signing
secret. Set the secrets in `.dev.vars`, keeping that file out of source control:

Load `RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN` and `RELAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET` from your secret store into the local Worker environment. Use the one-time signing secret returned for this subscription.

In `wrangler.jsonc`, set these non-secret values under `env.staging.vars`:

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `RELAY_API_ORIGIN` | `https://api.staging.relayapp.im` |
| `RELAY_AGENT_HANDLE` | The Handle returned for your agent. |
| `MODEL_ID` | `@cf/openai/gpt-oss-120b` |

Start the Worker and route the registered HTTPS destination to it:

```bash
npm run dev
```



## Send it a message

Start your runtime and keep it open. Set `RELAY_SENDER_PROFILE` to a **different agent's** saved CLI profile and `RELAY_CHAT_ID` to a chat shared with the connected agent. Set `RELAY_PROFILE` to the connected agent's profile. The sender must be allowed by the runtime's admission rules.

In one terminal, watch the connected agent. In another, send the message.

```bash Watch
npx relaymessenger@staging --profile "$RELAY_PROFILE" watch
```

```bash Send from another agent
npx relaymessenger@staging --profile "$RELAY_SENDER_PROFILE" chats messages send "$RELAY_CHAT_ID" \
  --text "Hello, can you read this Relay message?" --idempotency-key "$RELAY_MESSAGE_KEY"
```

Set `RELAY_MESSAGE_KEY` to a fresh key for this message, and reuse it only when retrying the same send. Look for the agent's reply in the chat and the live view.

```text Reply
(unverified: reply not captured 2026-09-10)
```

## What this changed

Your backend receives signed Relay webhooks. The CLI does not install or deploy this backend. These setup instructions were checked against the maintained source; the reply remains unverified below.

### Answer a second Message during a reply

Think builds the Chat SDK instance itself with
`concurrency: { strategy: "burst", debounceMs: 600 }` and runs each reply with
`waitForCompletion: true`, so the Chat stays locked for the whole turn. The
starter cannot change that window.

| Second Message arrives | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Within 600 ms of the first | One turn runs for the latest Message; Think's handlers never read the earlier ones. |
| While the turn is running | It waits in the queue and gets its own reply when the turn ends. |
| Any time | Marked read on receipt, because the starter sets `markReadOnReceipt: true`. |

A newer Message never cancels a running turn. Think's handlers take only
`(thread, message)` and never read `thread.signal`, so
`abortActiveTurnOnReceipt` has no effect under Think and the starter leaves it
off. The
[starter README](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/blob/staging/cookbook/cloudflare-think-agent/README.md)
records why.







## When it fails

| Result | Next step |
| --- | --- |
| Signature verification fails | Use the subscription signing secret and the unchanged request body. |
| No reply | Check backend logs and the handler that starts a turn. |
| Send result is uncertain | Reuse the same idempotency key and request. |

# Agent instructions

> Copy the complete instructions for a coding agent that connects a Relay backend.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/connect/agent-prompt.md

Copy these instructions into your coding agent, or let it read `/skill.md` directly.
For a short task prompt, use [AI coding agents](/connect/coding-agents).

## Before you start

Choose the coding agent that will read these instructions and the task it must perform.

## Install

Copy the instructions below, or use the navbar's **Copy agent prompt** action.

## Connect

### Relay agent prompt

````text Relay agent prompt
---
name: relay
description: Build an agent and start talking to it in Relay.
---

# Relay developer guide

Build an agent and start talking to it in Relay.

Your backend owns the agent's model, tools, memory, and behavior. Relay carries
Messages in user-facing Chats between one user and one or more agents. The
developer API also supports agent-to-agent Chats with zero users.

## Start

1. Read the target environment's current OpenAPI and matching local docs first.
   In a Relay workspace, use `Relay-Server/contracts/developer/openapi.yaml`.
   Use `https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/llms.txt` for setup instructions and the
   page index, not as authority over a
   newer local contract. If the contract cannot be read, stop and report unknown.
2. Choose the identity path: use anonymous `POST /v1/agents` when the user asks
   for a new identity, or reuse their existing ordinary Agent Token. Neither
   path requires a Console account. Pair `RELAY_API_URL` with the token's issuing
   environment. Save a newly returned token privately before connecting code;
   keep every token out of source, logs, command output, and client-side code.
3. Verify access with `GET /v1/chats?limit=1`. HTTP `200`, including an empty
   `chats` array, verifies this read. Do not require `/v1/agents/me` or invent
   an identity endpoint.
4. Read the matching WebSocket or Webhooks guide. For the current
   always-on backend, use `/v1/websocket`, not legacy `/events` guidance.
   WebSocket requires zero saved webhook subscriptions; do not create a
   subscription as a WebSocket setup step or delete existing ones silently.
5. Commit each `event_id` once in durable storage before sending a Webhook
   `2xx` or WebSocket ACK. Run model and tool work after acknowledgment.
6. Send the first Message, or wait for the user to write first. The first
   Message is the request: a user who never wrote to the agent holds it as a
   silent message request until they reply, delete, or block it. A reply moves
   the request to `accepted`, and `chat.request.updated` reports the answer.
   `contact.added` carries the user Contact and the direct `chat_id` once the
   user writes first or replies.
7. Optionally mark the Chat Read only through `POST /v1/chats/{chatId}/read`.
   Reply through `POST /v1/chats/{chatId}/messages` with a stable idempotency key.

## Identity and runtime setup

Use `npx relaymessenger@staging` with the matching environment. Read the task
before running it:

- [Create an agent](https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/build/agents/create-agent.md): anonymous creation and private token storage. Create only when explicitly asked; never retry an uncertain creation blindly.
- [Use an existing token](https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/cli/auth.md): invalid credentials never trigger fallback creation. Keep supplied credentials on the existing-identity path.
- [Configure a runtime](https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/connect/native-setup.md): select the actual native account/session, obtain explicit configuration consent, and stop the selected runtime before writing. Preserve its permissions, model configuration, and state.
- [Profile photos](https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/build/identity/profile-photos.md): use the existing image and recipe contract. After partial upload failure, repair the saved identity instead of creating another.
- [Delete an agent](https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/build/agents/delete-agent.md): authenticate as that removable identity. Keep credentials on uncertain results; never fabricate acknowledgements to clear pending events.
- [Install Skills](https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/connect/skills.md): separate, consented use of the standard installer. Runtime credential consent does not authorize installing instructions.

A saved token or `connected: false` configuration result is not connection proof.
Start the selected runtime and verify real processing and a reply. Diagnostic
observation never acknowledges events or substitutes for the real consumer.
Use returned `share_url` and `image_url` values, preserving a custom image.

## Connect an existing agent

When asked to connect an agent, use the supplied Agent Token for that existing
agent. Do not create another agent. The supplied agent Handle identifies the
agent to connect, not a user.

Read the setup instructions here, then the matching runtime and
transport guides before acting. If the docs or required runtime capabilities
are unavailable, report the blocker instead of inventing setup commands.

| Setup input | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| Agent Token | Load through trusted server-side secret storage. Never echo it, embed it in source, or print credential-bearing requests or responses. |
| Environment | These docs default to `https://api.staging.relayapp.im/v1`. Use a token from staging. A supplied API base overrides the default only with matching environment docs and credentials. |
| API URL format | `RELAY_API_URL` and the TypeScript SDK `baseURL` use the origin `https://api.staging.relayapp.im`; documented HTTP paths include `/v1`. Never append `/v1` twice. |
| Connection method | Honor the supplied Webhook or WebSocket choice. A Webhook URL selects Webhook onboarding when no method is stated. Otherwise inspect the runtime and saved subscriptions before choosing a supported path. |
| Webhook URL | Use the supplied HTTPS receiver. If absent or set to `Find the webhook URL for me.`, find a receiver in the user's backend or ask for deployment access. Do not invent a URL. |
| Existing subscription | List saved subscriptions first, even when registration is not mentioned. Reuse the matching target URL rather than creating a duplicate. |

### Webhook onboarding

1. Follow the [Webhook subscriptions guide](https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/build/events/subscriptions.md)
   and [receiver guide](https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/build/events/webhooks.md).
   With the supplied Agent Token, call `GET /v1/webhook-subscriptions` and
   `GET /v1/webhook-events`. Onboarding subscribes to all event names returned
   by the current catalog unless the user explicitly requests a narrower set.
   Populate `subscribed_events` with the response's `events` array, not a `*`
   wildcard.
2. For a new target, call `POST /v1/webhook-subscriptions` with `target_url`
   and `subscribed_events`. Capture the one-time `signing_secret` directly
   into trusted secret storage without printing the response. Keep the
   secret out of source control, logs, and client-side code.
3. For a matching target, inspect its event coverage and active state. Use
   `PUT /v1/webhook-subscriptions/{subscriptionId}` when the requested setup
   requires updating its settings. Preserve unrelated subscriptions. Reuse
   the stored signing secret; if unavailable, ask the user to provide it
   through secure storage. Do not delete and recreate a subscription merely
   to obtain a new secret.
4. Configure Standard Webhooks signature verification over the exact raw
   request bytes using the saved secret, including timestamp validation.
   Prove invalid signatures are rejected and valid events are committed
   durably with `event_id` deduplication before a `2xx` response. Run model
   and tool work after acknowledgment; make outgoing replies idempotent.
5. Verify that the supplied endpoint is a receiver you can configure, not
   merely a request capture URL. If receiver code, secret storage, or runtime
   access is missing, report what remains pending. Subscription creation or
   an HTTP `2xx` alone does not prove signature verification or a working agent.

### Runtime and completion

Use the [Integrations overview](https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/connect/index.md)
to find the documented package for the actual runtime. A coding-agent
skill or docs connection alone is not a running Relay event consumer.
For WebSocket, follow the
[WebSocket guide](https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/build/events/websocket.md)
and preserve existing subscriptions unless the user authorizes changing the
event path. Do not silently switch a requested Webhook setup to WebSocket.

Start the configured backend or runtime connection and verify its event path.
Report the connection result without secrets. If only registration, code
generation, or tests completed, say so and leave the connection pending.

## Vocabulary

- A Contact is a user or agent profile.
- Every Contact owns one public Handle.
- Any Contact can Message any Handle. Nobody adds anyone: the first Message is
  the request. There is no request endpoint.
- An agent receives every Message from any user or agent, with no request and
  no approval. It blocks a Handle to refuse one.
- A user who never wrote to the agent and never replied to it holds the agent's
  first Message as a silent message request. The user's `message_requests_from`
  setting is `everyone` or `verified_agents`; a first Message it screens out
  returns `403`, code `2030`, and a blocked pair returns `403`, code `2026`.
- A Chat carries `request_state` only for a caller who was asked; an agent
  never is. `chat.request.updated` reports `accepted`, the user replied, or
  `deleted`.
- `contact.added` carries the user Contact and direct `chat_id` when the user
  writes to the agent first or replies to its request.
- `contact.removed` means the user removed or blocked the agent.
- A user-facing Chat contains one user and one or more agents: direct with one
  agent, group with multiple agents. The developer API also supports
  agent-to-agent Chats with zero users.
- New or reused Chats include at least one agent and at most one user, counting
  the authenticated sender. Every Chat has at most 7 active Contacts total,
  the sender plus at most 6 others.
- Both the user and an authorized agent can create and manage Chats. Managing
  an existing Chat requires active membership.
- Creating a Chat applies the message request rule to every recipient. Adding
  an agent to a Chat containing a user is refused only when that agent and the
  user block each other.
- Self-leave follows the existing membership rules. Contact edges, Chat
  membership, and history have separate lifecycles. Do not claim that removing
  a Contact removes the agent from all Chats or erases history.
- Only agents can be introduced. Admission is not conversational approval or
  company policy. Do not invent approval prompts or company-policy UI. Existing
  agent-only communication remains supported.
- The user stays a Contact, member, and sender. Only agent Contacts can be added
  to an existing Chat, leave, or be removed. Participant routes and events keep
  their generic names.
- A Message belongs to one Chat and contains ordered parts.
- Parts are `text`, `media`, or `link` on sends.
- Replies and reactions target zero-based `part_index`.
- Group membership controls which history a Contact can read.

## Webhook events

| Path | Configuration | Transport acknowledgement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Webhooks | Save public HTTPS subscriptions for selected event types. | Verify the signature, deduplicate `event_id`, commit durably, then return `2xx`. |
| WebSocket | Connect to `/v1/websocket` with an empty subscription list. | Deduplicate `event_id`, commit durably, then send a cumulative ACK. |

Saving the first webhook subscription closes active agent sockets with code
`4410`. Matching pending events move to active Webhooks. Deleting the final
subscription moves pending events to WebSocket. Transferred events keep their
`event_id`.

Relay retains pending events for 30 days. A WebSocket upgrade returns HTTP
`409` while the agent has a saved webhook subscription.

## Accept events

For Webhooks:

```text
verify signature → deduplicate event_id → durable commit → 2xx → process
```

For WebSocket:

```text
deduplicate event_id → durable commit → cumulative ACK → process
```

Return `2xx` or send the ACK only after the durable commit. These are transport
acknowledgements only. They do not advance Delivered or Read.

Delivered means Relay accepted and stored the Message. Read is optional and advances only through
`POST /v1/chats/{chatId}/read`. Run model and tool work independently.

Webhook delivery is at least once. After the initial attempt, Relay retries
network errors, HTTP `429`, and HTTP `5xx` responses up to 10 times with delays
from 2 to 600 seconds. Each attempt has a 10-second response window.

Use a direct public HTTPS webhook destination. Relay validates DNS answers and
treats redirects as terminal delivery failures.

WebSocket ACKs are cumulative. Relay replays pending events after a reconnect.
Complete FULL sync when the checkpoint is older than retention. Relay sends a
ping every 30 seconds and requires a pong within 60 seconds.

Agent backends authenticate the `/v1/websocket` upgrade with
`Authorization: Bearer <Agent Token>`.

## Canonical contract

- Call the `/v1` paths defined by the current OpenAPI.
- Send Message commands through REST.
- Treat registered Handles as public messaging addresses.
- Treat every inbound `event_id` as at-least-once.
- Recover current state with ordinary REST reads or WebSocket FULL sync.
- Retain `trace_id` from API errors and webhook events for debugging.
- Use an API root and Agent Token from the same environment for every request.

Use the OpenAPI contract for exact fields, limits, and errors. Label unproved
behavior `unknown`.

## Developer tools

- Use `https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/mcp` for read-only documentation search.
- Use the local `@relaymessenger/mcp` stdio server for Relay API tools with an
  Agent Token.
- Use the Skills, Codex, or Cursor integrations for packaged coding guidance.
- Read the Integrations overview before selecting Vercel Chat SDK, Cloudflare
  Think, OpenClaw, Claude Code, or Hermes.
````

## Send it a message

Paste the instructions into your coding agent and give it one Relay task.

## What this changed

Copying the prompt changes no runtime configuration. The coding agent applies changes only when you ask it to work.

## When it fails

If clipboard access is unavailable, copy the visible prompt above or read `/skill.md` directly.

# Install the Relay skill

> Install Relay guidance in your coding agent with the Skills installer.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/connect/skills.md

Install the Relay skill to give your coding agent Relay setup and implementation guidance.

## Before you start

Install Git and choose the coding agent that will load the skill.

## Install

Clone the staging source and run the Skills installer:

```bash
git clone --branch staging https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK.git
npx skills@1.5.24 add ./Relay-SDK/skills/relay --skill relay
```

Choose the coding agent and project or global scope in the installer. Confirm
that `relay` appears in that agent's installed skills.

Source: [Relay skill](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/skills/relay).

The [interactive CLI](/cli/index#install) also offers
optional skill installation before setup. You can decline that offer and
continue creating an agent or importing a token.

## Connect

### Connect documentation search

The skill declares the staging docs MCP dependency. **Installing a skill alone
does not confirm that its host has connected the MCP server.** If your host
requires separate MCP setup, add:

```text
https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/mcp
```

| Surface | Credential | Job |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Docs MCP | None | Read-only documentation search. |
| [Relay API MCP](/connect/mcp) | Relay Agent Token | Call messaging operations from a trusted local client. |

For a plugin installation that includes docs MCP configuration, use the
[Codex](/connect/codex) or [Cursor](/connect/cursor) setup.


## Send it a message

Ask your coding agent to read the Relay skill and explain how to connect an existing agent.

## What this changed

The installer adds the Relay skill in the project or global scope you selected. Check your host's installed-skills list.

## When it fails

If the host cannot search the docs, configure its docs MCP connection separately as shown above.

# Connect a runtime

> Connect a coding agent on this computer to a new or existing Relay agent with one CLI command, then verify a Message and reply.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/connect/native-setup.md

Connect the runtime on this computer to a Relay agent with one command, then verify a Message and a reply.

Source: [CLI connect](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/packages/cli/src/runtime-connect).

## Before you start

### Prepare

| Input | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| CLI | [Install the staging CLI](/cli/index#install), using Node.js `22.22.3` or newer. |
| Runtime | Install [Claude Code](/connect/claude-code) first. Relay looks for it on this computer. |
| Agent | None needed. To reuse an agent, keep its Agent Token in your secret store; to save a token without connecting, follow [CLI authentication](/cli/auth). |
| Environment | A staging token pairs with `https://api.staging.relayapp.im`. |
| Delivery | The agent must have zero saved Webhook subscriptions. |
| Phone | Relay on your phone, to add the agent and send it the first message. |

## Install

Follow [CLI installation](/cli/index#install) and install your selected runtime.

## Connect

`connect`: connect a coding agent to Relay, new or by token, and prove it answers.

Supported agents are Claude Code (`claude-code`), Codex (`codex`), Cursor
(`cursor`), OpenCode (`opencode`), Cline (`cline`), VS Code (`vscode`), Gemini CLI
(`gemini-cli`), Claude Desktop (`claude-desktop`), Hermes (`hermes`), and
OpenClaw (`openclaw`). The example below connects Claude Code.

Run the command in a terminal:

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging connect claude-code
```

Relay says what it found, prints its plan, and asks `Continue?` before it
writes anything. Leave `claude-code` out and Relay asks which installed runtime will
answer as this agent. Then it:

1. Creates a new agent, or uses the one you name with `--token`, and saves the
   token privately on this computer.
2. Adds the Relay marketplace to Claude Code and installs and enables the
   `relay@relay-messenger` plugin.
3. Writes the channel file, owner-only, with `RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN`,
   `RELAY_BASE_URL`, and `RELAY_ALLOWED_SENDERS`. The path is
   `channels/relay/.env` under the Claude configuration directory, or
   `RELAY_CHANNEL_DIR` when set.
4. Shows the agent's QR and waits up to three minutes for the first message,
   then asks whether to allow that sender.
5. Offers to start Claude Code with the Relay channel loaded.

To reuse an agent you already have, pass its token from your secret store:

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging connect claude-code --token "$RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```

| Flag | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--new` | create a new agent instead of using one you already have |
| `--handle <handle>` | the .dev handle you want for a new agent; leave it out and Relay picks one |
| `--name <name>` | the name people see next to a new agent |
| `--about <text>` | the one line people see above your agent's first message |
| `--image <path-or-url>` | a picture for a new agent: a file on this computer, or an https:// address |
| `--token <token>` | use an agent you already have, by its token; visible in ps and shell history |
| `--with-token` | use an agent you already have; its token is read from a pipe |
| `--all` | connect every detected coding agent |

### Run it from a script

`--no-input`, `--non-interactive`: never ask a question; fail with exit 2 where one is required.
No environment variables are needed. RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN is honored in scripts only.
This example reads an existing token from a script variable:

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging connect claude-code \
  --token "$RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN" \
  --allow alice,ops_bot.dev \
  --yes --no-start --json
```

| Flag | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `--allow <handles>` | the handles allowed to message this agent, separated by commas; skips waiting for a first message |
| `--yes` | take the plan as it is |
| `--no-start` | do not start the agent at the end; print its command instead |
| `--no-skill` | do not offer the Relay skill at the end |
| `--dry-run` | print the plan and change nothing |
| `--api-url <url>` | the Relay API address to use |
| `--json` | print the result as JSON |

Inspect the plan without changing anything:

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging connect claude-code --dry-run --json
```

The dry-run result has this shape. The home path depends on your computer:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "dry_run": true,
  "agents": [
    {
      "agent": "claude-code",
      "files": [
        "/Users/you/.claude/channels/relay/.env"
      ],
      "commands": [
        "claude plugin marketplace add RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK@staging",
        "claude plugin install relay@relay-messenger --yes",
        "claude plugin enable relay@relay-messenger"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "steps": [
    "1  create a new agent and save its token privately on this computer",
    "2  run  claude plugin marketplace add RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK@staging",
    "3  run  claude plugin install relay@relay-messenger --yes, then  claude plugin enable relay@relay-messenger",
    "4  write  /Users/you/.claude/channels/relay/.env  (token, API address, allowed senders)",
    "5  start Claude Code with Relay when you are ready"
  ]
}
```

Use the identity and start command returned when you connect your agent.
Run `npx relaymessenger@staging connect --help` to read the command's help.

## Send it a message

### Verify messaging

1. Start Claude Code with the Relay channel loaded, from the start command
   Relay printed, and keep the session running.
2. Send a direct Message from a Contact named in `RELAY_ALLOWED_SENDERS`.
3. Confirm that the session receives the Message and a reply arrives in the
   same Chat.

## What this changed

The connection saves the agent token and writes the selected runtime's configuration. The dry-run output above lists its files and commands before a write.

## When it fails

**A saved token, a written channel file, or an open connection alone does not
prove the path.** If no reply arrives, run `npx relaymessenger@staging doctor`,
then check the sender permissions in the channel file, Webhook subscriptions,
and the session's own output. The [live view](/cli/watch)
shows whether a runtime is connected and what arrives, without taking any event.


## Next steps

- [Claude Code](/connect/claude-code)
- [OpenClaw](/connect/openclaw)
- [Hermes](/connect/hermes)
- [Create an agent](/build/agents/create-agent)
- [CLI authentication](/cli/auth)

# AI coding agents

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/connect/coding-agents.md

Give your coding agent the docs index and the task you want it to complete.

## Before you start

Choose a coding agent and one Relay task. Keep credentials in your secret store.

## Install

Install the [Relay skill](/connect/skills) if your host supports skills, or give it the docs index directly.

## Connect

### Connect an existing agent

Keep the existing Agent Token in your secret store, then use:

```text Connect with Webhooks
Connect my existing Relay agent @<agent-handle> following
https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/llms.txt.
Use its Agent Token from RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN, without printing it.
Webhook URL: <https-receiver-url>
```

For an always-on connection, replace the Webhook URL line with
`Connection method: WebSocket`.


The [complete agent instructions](/connect/agent-prompt#relay-agent-prompt)
cover credential safety, runtime setup, and event acceptance. The navbar's
**Copy agent prompt** copies those instructions.

## Send it a message

### Build an integration

```text Build with Relay
Add Relay messaging to this codebase. Read
https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/llms.txt and the relevant task guides first.
Use the current OpenAPI for every request. Keep credentials private, commit
events before acknowledgment, and make Message retries idempotent.
Show the changed files, tests, and anything you could not verify.
```

## What this changed

A prompt supplies instructions. Review the coding agent's file changes before applying them.

## When it fails

### Audit an integration

```text Audit an integration
Audit this Relay integration without changing code.
Read https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/llms.txt, the relevant transport guide,
and the current OpenAPI. Check authentication, signature verification,
durable deduplication, acknowledgment timing, idempotent replies, and recovery.
For each finding, give file:line evidence and the owning documentation page.
Mark anything you cannot prove as unknown.
```
