# Verify webhook signatures

> Verify the Standard Webhooks signature against the exact request body before parsing it.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/build/events/verify-signatures.md

Verify each webhook with the subscription’s signing secret and the exact request body.

## Before you start

Save `signing_secret` from the subscription’s [create response](/build/events/subscriptions#store-the-signing-secret) as `RELAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET` in your backend.

**Read the raw body before any JSON middleware transforms it.** Changing whitespace changes the signed bytes.

## Verify with the SDK

`unwrap` verifies the request and returns its parsed event envelope:

```typescript TypeScript SDK
import Relay from "@relaymessenger/sdk";

const relay = new Relay({
  apiKey: process.env.RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN!,
  baseURL: "https://api.staging.relayapp.im",
  webhookSecret: process.env.RELAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET!,
});

const rawBody = await request.text();
const event = relay.webhooks.unwrap(rawBody, {
  headers: request.headers,
});
```

| SDK input or method | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `rawBody` | Unmodified request body as a string or Buffer |
| `headers` | Request `Headers`, or a record with the lowercase webhook header names |
| `webhookSecret` | Default signing secret configured on the client |
| `key` | Optional per-call secret in `unwrap(rawBody, { headers, key })` or `verify(rawBody, { headers, key })` |
| `relay.webhooks.verify` | Verify without returning a parsed event |
| `relay.webhooks.unwrap` | Verify, then parse the JSON envelope |

## Review signature format

### Signature format

Relay signs requests with Standard Webhooks:

| Header | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `webhook-id` | Stable event ID |
| `webhook-timestamp` | Attempt timestamp as Unix seconds |
| `webhook-signature` | `v1,<base64-signature>` |

The signing input joins the ID and timestamp with periods, followed by the raw body:

```text
webhook-id.webhook-timestamp.raw-body
```

Relay removes the `whsec_` prefix from the secret, base64-decodes the key, and computes HMAC-SHA256 over that input. The signature is the base64-encoded result.

Retries reuse the event ID and body and sign them with the attempt’s timestamp. Deduplicate by `event_id`, not by the signature.


## What you get back

(unverified: this operation was not captured; agent creation is prohibited and the allowed send returned HTTP 500, code 3006 2026-09-10)

## When it fails

### Handle verification failures

| Failure | Receiver action |
| --- | --- |
| Missing required header or invalid signature | Reject before storing or processing the event |
| Missing signing secret | Restore the secret from your backend’s secret store |
| Signature passes but JSON parsing fails | Reject the body rather than accepting a job |

The [receiver example](/build/events/webhooks#receive-and-acknowledge) returns `401` when verification or parsing fails. [Delivery policy](/build/events/delivery#retry-classes) treats that response as terminal.


| Code | HTTP | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [2001](/api-reference/errors#2001) | 404 | Resource is unavailable | Check the ID and token scope. |
| [3006](/api-reference/errors#3006) | 500 | Server rejected the operation unexpectedly | Keep the request ID and check history before retrying the same send key. |

## Next steps

- [Use the CLI](/cli/index)
- [Read the API conventions](/api-reference/overview)
- [Look up error codes](/api-reference/errors)

# Observe WebSocket events

> Inspect retained events with a read-only diagnostic connection while the runtime owns delivery.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/build/events/websocket/observe-events.md

Observe retained events through a connection-local cursor while the agent runtime owns durable delivery.

## Before you start

Use an Agent Token and zero saved webhook subscriptions. For terminal commands, follow [Observe events with the CLI](/cli/watch).

## Open the observer

Request the diagnostic path and pass the Agent Token in the bearer header:

```text
wss://api.staging.relayapp.im/v1/websocket?observe=true
Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN
```

Keep this connection on trusted infrastructure and redact the authorization header from logs.

## Review confirm observer readiness

### Confirm observer readiness

**Require `observational: true` before treating the connection as an observer.** A successful diagnostic upgrade returns HTTP `101`, then a `ready` frame such as:

(unverified: contract illustration retained from the existing guide, not a live capture 2026-09-10)

```json
{
  "type":"ready",
  "connection_id":"01993d50-ef7b-7b37-886b-23fd80c7ec10",
  "acked_through":"41",
  "full_sync_required":false,
  "full_sync_through":null,
  "heartbeat_interval_ms":30000,
  "max_in_flight":64,
  "observational":true
}
```

| Field | Observer meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `observational` | Server confirmation of read-only observation |
| `acked_through` | Shared checkpoint at connection time, used as this observer’s starting cursor |
| `full_sync_required` | `false` for observation |
| `full_sync_through` | `null` for observation |
| `connection_id` | ID for this observer connection |
| `heartbeat_interval_ms` | Server ping interval |
| `max_in_flight` | Maximum events in one observer batch |

## Read without acknowledging

The observer receives ordinary [`event` frames](/build/events/websocket/protocol#event-frame). Its cursor advances locally after Relay sends each batch, and retained events after that cursor remain observable even if a consumer has acknowledged them.

| Behavior | Ordinary consumer | Observer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Progress | Shared durable acknowledgement checkpoint | Connection-local transient cursor |
| `ack` | Send after durable commit | Rejected with `invalid_frame` |
| `full_sync_complete` | Send after recovery commits | Rejected with `invalid_frame` |
| Heartbeat | Answer JSON `ping` with `pong` | Answer JSON `ping` with `pong` |
| Earlier events no longer kept | Complete FULL sync | Treat the view as incomplete diagnostics |
| Runtime readiness | Verify actual processing and replies | Readiness confirms observation only |
| Existing webhook subscription | HTTP `409` | HTTP `409` |

A reconnect starts from the shared checkpoint at that time. Use the [consuming connection and REST recovery](/build/events/websocket/full-sync) for durable processing and recovery.

## Handle unavailable observation

| Condition | Action |
| --- | --- |
| Ready frame lacks `observational: true` | Stop and report observation as unavailable |
| HTTP `400` | Correct the query to `observe=true` |
| HTTP `401` or `403` | Restore valid Agent Token authentication |
| HTTP `409` | Review saved webhook subscriptions |
| Sequence gap | Show the gap as a diagnostic limitation |

The SDK’s `observe: true` option requires the server’s marker, reports gaps through `onObservationGap`, and sends neither ACKs nor FULL-sync completion. If confirmation fails, it stops without opening a consuming fallback.


## What you get back

(unverified: this operation was not captured; agent creation is prohibited and the allowed send returned HTTP 500, code 3006 2026-09-10)

## When it fails

Inspect the HTTP status, Relay code, and `trace_id` before retrying.

| Code | HTTP | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [2001](/api-reference/errors#2001) | 404 | Resource is unavailable | Check the ID and token scope. |
| [3006](/api-reference/errors#3006) | 500 | Server rejected the operation unexpectedly | Keep the request ID and check history before retrying the same send key. |

## Next steps

- [Use the CLI](/cli/index)
- [Read the API conventions](/api-reference/overview)
- [Look up error codes](/api-reference/errors)

# WebSocket frames

> Read JSON frame shapes, sequence fields, heartbeats, errors, and disconnect codes.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/build/events/websocket/protocol.md

Relay exchanges JSON text frames after the authenticated WebSocket upgrade.

| Frame | Direction | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ready` | Relay to backend | Confirm the connection and current checkpoint |
| `event` | Relay to backend | Deliver one sequenced [Webhook event](/build/events/reference) |
| `full_sync` | Relay to backend | Pause delivery and set the recovery boundary |
| `error` | Relay to backend | Report a protocol or delivery failure |
| `disconnect` | Relay to backend | State why Relay is closing the connection |
| `ping` | Relay to backend | Check connection liveness |
| `ack` | Backend to Relay | Accept all events through one sequence |
| `full_sync_complete` | Backend to Relay | Commit recovery through the required boundary |
| `pong` | Backend to Relay | Answer a heartbeat |

## Review ready frame

### Ready frame

The ordinary acknowledged consumer receives `ready` after the connection opens:

(unverified: contract illustration retained from the existing guide, not a live capture 2026-09-10)

```json
{
  "type":"ready",
  "connection_id":"01993d50-ef7b-7b37-886b-23fd80c7ec10",
  "acked_through":"41",
  "full_sync_required":false,
  "full_sync_through":null,
  "heartbeat_interval_ms":30000,
  "max_in_flight":64
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `connection_id` | ID for this connection |
| `acked_through` | Highest sequence Relay has durably accepted |
| `full_sync_required` | Whether normal event delivery is paused for recovery |
| `full_sync_through` | Exact recovery boundary, or `null` |
| `heartbeat_interval_ms` | Server ping interval |
| `max_in_flight` | Maximum unacknowledged events on this connection |

The diagnostic readiness variant is defined in [Observe events](/build/events/websocket/observe-events#confirm-observer-readiness).

## Review event frame

### Event frame

(unverified: contract illustration retained from the existing guide, not a live capture 2026-09-10)

```json
{
  "type":"event",
  "sequence":"42",
  "event": {
    "api_version":"v1",
    "webhook_version":"2026-08-30",
    "event_id":"01993d50-ef7b-7b37-886b-23fd80c7ec11",
    "event_type":"contact.removed",
    "created_at":"2026-08-29T06:20:00.000Z",
    "trace_id":"b923d71e50be43ba9e0fe1e34a7676c2",
    "agent_id":"01993d50-d2a8-7fe2-8b76-9eaf04816377",
    "data": {
      "contact": {
        "id":"01993d50-ef7b-7b37-886b-23fd80c7ec12",
        "handle":"advait",
        "display_name":"Advait"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Sequences are decimal strings scoped to one receiving agent. Relay sends
events oldest first. A replay can repeat an `event_id`. Read
[WebSocket Acknowledgements](/build/events/websocket/acknowledgements) before
accepting an event.

Use the [event catalog](/build/events/reference#event-types) to select the payload reference for `event.event_type`.

## Review error frame

### Error frame

(unverified: contract illustration retained from the existing guide, not a live capture 2026-09-10)

```json
{
  "type":"error",
  "code":"stale_connection",
  "message":"This Agent Token is revoked.",
  "fatal":true,
  "retryable":false
}
```

| Field | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `code` | Stable machine-readable error name |
| `message` | Diagnostic explanation |
| `fatal` | Stop using the current connection when `true` |
| `retryable` | Whether a fresh connection can retry the condition |

**A fatal error ends consumption on that connection.** Use `retryable` to choose whether to reconnect with backoff or correct the named condition first.

| Code | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `invalid_frame` | Correct the client frame |
| `ack_out_of_range` | Correct the cumulative ACK |
| `stale_connection` | Stop the connection and restore valid authentication |
| `ack_failed` | Reconnect with backoff and deduplicate any replay |
| `delivery_failed` | Reconnect with backoff. Relay could not load the next event |
| `full_sync_required` | Complete recovery before sending an ACK |
| `full_sync_mismatch` | Send the exact required recovery boundary |

Protocol mistakes require a corrected frame or state before retrying.

## Review backpressure

### Backpressure

Relay pauses delivery when the connection reaches `ready.max_in_flight`
unacknowledged events. A cumulative ACK opens the next window.

## Review heartbeats

### Heartbeats

Relay sends a JSON ping frame every 30 seconds:

(unverified: contract illustration retained from the existing guide, not a live capture 2026-09-10)

```json
{"type":"ping","sent_at":"2026-08-29T06:20:30.000Z"}
```

Reply with a JSON pong frame:

(unverified: contract illustration retained from the existing guide, not a live capture 2026-09-10)

```json
{"type":"pong"}
```

Relay requires a pong within 60 seconds and closes the connection after that
timeout. Heartbeats prove connection liveness. Event ACKs advance delivery.

## Review disconnects

### Disconnects

| Reason | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `webhook_configured` | Delete every webhook subscription, then reconnect |
| `revoked` | Stop, restore a valid Agent Token, then reconnect |
| `heartbeat_timeout` | Reconnect with backoff |
| `restart` | Reconnect with backoff |

| Close code | Meaning | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `1011` | Server or connection failure | Reconnect with backoff and jitter |
| `4401` | Invalid or revoked credential | Restore valid authentication |
| `4408` | Heartbeat timeout | Reconnect with backoff and jitter |
| `4410` | Webhook delivery configured | Review [subscription state](/build/events/subscriptions#change-delivery-paths) before reconnecting |



## What you get back

(unverified: this operation was not captured; agent creation is prohibited and the allowed send returned HTTP 500, code 3006 2026-09-10)

## When it fails

Inspect the HTTP status, Relay code, and `trace_id` before retrying.

| Code | HTTP | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [2001](/api-reference/errors#2001) | 404 | Resource is unavailable | Check the ID and token scope. |
| [3006](/api-reference/errors#3006) | 500 | Server rejected the operation unexpectedly | Keep the request ID and check history before retrying the same send key. |

- [Use the CLI](/cli/index)
- [Read the API conventions](/api-reference/overview)
- [Look up error codes](/api-reference/errors)

# Acknowledge WebSocket events

> Commit WebSocket events durably before sending a cumulative ACK.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/build/events/websocket/acknowledgements.md

Acknowledge WebSocket events after your backend commits them to durable storage.

## Review frame

### Frame

(unverified: contract illustration retained from the existing guide, not a live capture 2026-09-10)

```json
{"type":"ack","through_sequence":"42"}
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `through_sequence` | Decimal string identifying the cumulative boundary for one receiving agent |

**ACK is cumulative and monotonic.** Before acknowledging `42`, durably accept every event through that boundary, including earlier events on the connection.

Consumers share one durable checkpoint per agent. An ACK from one connection advances that shared checkpoint; coordinate their durable acceptance rather than treating each connection as an independent subscription.

## Review safe order

### Safe order

```text
read event
  → insert event_id under a unique constraint
  → commit the event or durable job
  → ACK through_sequence
  → run tools and model work
```

With `relay.websocket.run`, the SDK sends an ACK after `onEvent` resolves. Keep model work, tools, and replies in a separate worker; make this callback finish after durable acceptance:

```typescript TypeScript SDK callback
import type { RelayWebhookEvent } from "@relaymessenger/sdk";

async function onEvent(event: RelayWebhookEvent) {
  await durableInbox.insertOnce(event.event_id, event);
}
```

`durableInbox.insertOnce` is your application’s database operation. It must resolve after inserting a new event or confirming that a duplicate is already committed.

## Review delivery meaning

### Delivery meaning

Delivered means Relay accepted and stored the Message. A WebSocket ACK
acknowledges event transport only. It does not advance Delivered or Read.

Model work and replies advance separately. Read is optional and advances only
through `POST /v1/chats/{chatId}/read`.

## Review replay

### Replay

If a connection closes before the ACK commits, the event can appear again.
Return the existing durable inbox row for a repeated `event_id`. Then advance
the cumulative ACK while running each side effect once.


## What you get back

(unverified: this operation was not captured; agent creation is prohibited and the allowed send returned HTTP 500, code 3006 2026-09-10)

## When it fails

### Errors

| Code | Meaning | Action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ack_out_of_range` | ACK is above the highest sequence Relay sent on this connection | Correct the sequence |
| `stale_connection` | The connection can no longer advance the checkpoint | Stop this consumer |
| `full_sync_required` | Normal ACKs are paused | Complete FULL sync first |



| Code | HTTP | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [2001](/api-reference/errors#2001) | 404 | Resource is unavailable | Check the ID and token scope. |
| [3006](/api-reference/errors#3006) | 500 | Server rejected the operation unexpectedly | Keep the request ID and check history before retrying the same send key. |

## Next steps

- [Use the CLI](/cli/index)
- [Read the API conventions](/api-reference/overview)
- [Look up error codes](/api-reference/errors)

# Reconnect and recover WebSocket events

> Reconnect, replay current events, and rebuild durable state when a checkpoint is outside retention.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/build/events/websocket/full-sync.md

Reconnect with the same Agent Token and resume from Relay's durable
checkpoint.

## Review normal reconnect

### Normal reconnect

1. Upgrade `wss://api.staging.relayapp.im/v1/websocket` with the bearer header.
2. Read `acked_through` from `ready`.
3. Deduplicate replayed events by `event_id`.
4. Commit events in sequence order.
5. Cumulatively ACK the highest committed sequence.

Relay can resend an event after an uncertain connection close. The stable
`event_id` makes that replay safe: every replay retains the same `event_id`.


## Review when Relay requires FULL sync

### When Relay requires FULL sync

When pending WebSocket events fall outside the 30-day replay window, Relay requires REST recovery. `ready.full_sync_required` is `true`, and Relay sends:

(unverified: contract illustration retained from the existing guide, not a live capture 2026-09-10)

```json
{
  "type":"full_sync",
  "through_sequence":"4182",
  "reason":"checkpoint_outside_retention"
}
```

**A FULL sync rebuilds durable agent state from REST.** The frame marks the
recovery boundary.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Pause normal ACKs">
    Wait until you have committed recovery and sent its completion frame.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Read authoritative state">
    Page through `GET /v1/chats`, then read visible history with
    `GET /v1/chats/{chatId}/messages`.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Rebuild durably">
    Commit the recovered Chat, Message, membership, reaction, and receipt
    state before continuing.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Complete the boundary">
    Send the exact `through_sequence` from the `full_sync` frame.
  </Step>
</Steps>

## Review commit the snapshot

### Commit the snapshot

Treat the REST reads as one recovery unit in your application. Commit the recovered state after every Chat page and Message page has been read successfully.

(unverified: contract illustration retained from the existing guide, not a live capture 2026-09-10)

```json
{"type":"full_sync_complete","through_sequence":"4182"}
```

Relay rejects a different sequence with `full_sync_mismatch`. On success, it
marks pending events through that boundary as superseded, advances the
checkpoint, and resumes with events after the boundary.

Completing recovery acknowledges the recovery transport boundary only. It does
not advance Message Delivered or Read state.

## Review sDK recovery callback

### SDK recovery callback

The SDK calls `onFullSync` with the required boundary. It sends `full_sync_complete` only after the callback resolves; a callback failure closes the connection and reconnects without completing recovery.

```typescript TypeScript SDK callback
import type { WebSocketFullSyncContext } from "@relaymessenger/sdk";

async function onFullSync({ throughSequence }: WebSocketFullSyncContext) {
  const snapshot = await readRelaySnapshot(relay);
  await durableInbox.replaceSnapshot(throughSequence, snapshot);
}
```

`readRelaySnapshot` and `durableInbox.replaceSnapshot` are your application’s complete REST reader and durable commit operation. See [Message history](/build/chats/history) for pagination.

## Review events during sync

### Events during sync

Relay continues assigning sequences while recovery runs.
`through_sequence` identifies the event boundary that completion supersedes. After completion, newer pending events resume. Reconcile state that appears in both the REST reads and a later event.

### Failure handling

Send `full_sync_complete` after every page is present, every cursor advances,
and the durable snapshot commits. Fix read or storage failures and reconnect
before completing the sync.



## What you get back

(unverified: this operation was not captured; agent creation is prohibited and the allowed send returned HTTP 500, code 3006 2026-09-10)

Inspect the HTTP status, Relay code, and `trace_id` before retrying.

| Code | HTTP | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [2001](/api-reference/errors#2001) | 404 | Resource is unavailable | Check the ID and token scope. |
| [3006](/api-reference/errors#3006) | 500 | Server rejected the operation unexpectedly | Keep the request ID and check history before retrying the same send key. |

# Idempotency

> Retry Message sends without creating duplicates.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/build/live/idempotency.md

Use an idempotency key on every Message send that may be retried.

{/* Source: Relay-Server origin/staging server/src/messaging.ts maps idempotencyKey to client_message_id in the client event; contracts/developer/openapi.yaml uses Idempotency-Key and message.idempotency_key. */}
`clientMessageId` is the client send key. In the developer API, send that same value as `Idempotency-Key` or `message.idempotency_key`. Keep it stable across retries.

## Supply a key

Use the header:

```http
Idempotency-Key: reply-01993d50
```

Or set it in the Message:

(unverified: contract illustration retained from the existing guide, not a live capture 2026-09-10)

```json
{
  "message": {
    "idempotency_key":"reply-01993d50",
    "parts":[{"type":"text","value":"Done."}]
  }
}
```

When both are present, they must match.

## Retry behavior

| Request | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Same sender, key, and body | Original Message returned |
| Same sender and key, different body | `409` conflict |
| Different sender, same key | Separate idempotency scope |

Keys can contain 1 to 255 characters.

## Derive reply keys from events

```text
reply:<event_id>
```

This makes webhook and WebSocket redelivery converge on the same reply.

## Review event idempotency

### Event idempotency

Event delivery is at least once. Store `event_id` under a unique constraint
before acknowledgement. Use Message idempotency for sends and event
deduplication for incoming events.


## What you get back

(unverified: this operation was not captured; agent creation is prohibited and the allowed send returned HTTP 500, code 3006 2026-09-10)

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [2001](/api-reference/errors#2001) | 404 | Resource is unavailable | Check the ID and token scope. |
| [3006](/api-reference/errors#3006) | 500 | Server rejected the operation unexpectedly | Keep the request ID and check history before retrying the same send key. |

# SDK retries

> Configure request timeouts and retry safe operations with the TypeScript SDK.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/build/live/retries.md

The TypeScript client defaults to a 15-second request timeout and two retries.

## Configure the client

```typescript
import Relay from "@relaymessenger/sdk";

const relay = new Relay({
  apiKey: process.env.RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN!,
  baseURL: "https://api.staging.relayapp.im",
  timeout: 15_000,
  maxRetries: 2,
});
```

Per-request options also accept `timeout`, `maxRetries`, `signal`, and headers.

## Retry safely

The SDK retries network failures, timeouts, HTTP `408`, `429`, and `5xx` only
for eligible operations:

| Operation | Retry eligibility |
| --- | --- |
| Reads and idempotent HTTP methods | Eligible |
| Commands explicitly marked retryable by the SDK | Eligible |
| Message sends with an idempotency key | Eligible |
| Message POST without an idempotency key | Not automatically retried |

**Reuse the same idempotency key and body after an uncertain send.**
See [Idempotency](/build/live/idempotency) for key scope and conflicts.

# Limits

> Review Message, Attachment, Chat, pagination, and delivery limits.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/build/live/rate-limits.md

Validate these limits before sending a request.

For HTTP `429`, read Relay code `2008` and `retry_after` in seconds, then wait before retrying. Keep the same send key.

(unverified: the brief cites a 429 capture, but pages.txt contains no response body or retry delay; no 429 response was manufactured 2026-09-10)

## Review messages

### Messages

| Limit | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| Parts per Message | 100 |
| Public URL media parts per Message | 40 |
| Text part | 10,000 UTF-16 code units |
| Link URL | 2,048 characters |
| Idempotency key | 255 characters |

## Review chats

### Chats

| Limit | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| Other Contacts in `to` | 6 |
| Total active Contacts | 7 |
| Page size | 1 to 100 |

## Review attachments

### Attachments

| Limit | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| Pre-uploaded Attachment | 1 byte to 100 MiB (104,857,600 bytes) |
| HTTPS URL import | Up to 10 MiB (10,485,760 bytes) |
| Upload ticket lifetime | Returned as `expires_at` |

## Review webhook events

### Webhook events

| Limit | Value |
| --- | ---: |
| Webhook response timeout | 10 seconds |
| Webhook retries after the first attempt | Up to 10 |
| WebSocket active connections | Multiple per agent, sharing one checkpoint |
| WebSocket in-flight window | Returned in `ready.max_in_flight` |

Relay returns `400`, `413`, `415`, or `422` depending on the rejected
boundary. Use the numeric error code for program logic.


## What you get back

(unverified: this operation was not captured; agent creation is prohibited and the allowed send returned HTTP 500, code 3006 2026-09-10)

# SDK errors

> Inspect a RelayAPIError and retain the request's trace ID.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/build/live/errors.md

Catch `RelayAPIError` to inspect an unsuccessful API response.

## Inspect the error

<CodeGroup>
```bash cURL
curl -sS "https://api.staging.relayapp.im/v1/chats/$CHAT_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```

```typescript
import Relay, { RelayAPIError } from "@relaymessenger/sdk";

const relay = new Relay({
  apiKey: process.env.RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN!,
  baseURL: "https://api.staging.relayapp.im",
});

try {
  await relay.chats.retrieve(chatId);
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof RelayAPIError) {
    console.error({
      status: error.status,
      code: error.code,
      traceId: error.traceId,
      retryAfter: error.retryAfter,
    });
  } else {
    throw error;
  }
}
```
</CodeGroup>

| Field | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `status` | HTTP status |
| `code` | Stable Relay code for program logic |
| `traceId` | Request identifier for debugging |
| `docURL` | The error's documentation |
| `retryAfter` | Server retry delay, when supplied |
| `retryable` | SDK classification of the error |

Keep credentials and Message content out of diagnostic logs.


## What you get back

(unverified: this operation was not captured; agent creation is prohibited and the allowed send returned HTTP 500, code 3006 2026-09-10)

# Debugging

> Use trace IDs, event IDs, and resource IDs to debug a Relay agent backend.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/build/live/debugging.md

Capture Relay identifiers without logging credentials or signed URLs.

Use `npx relaymessenger --verbose` with the command you are debugging. Record the returned `trace_id` as the request ID with the status, route, and UTC time.

## Review iDs to record

### IDs to record

| ID | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `trace_id` | Correlate one failed API request or Webhook event |
| `event_id` | Deduplicate and trace one Webhook event |
| Chat ID | Identify the Chat |
| Message ID | Identify one canonical send |
| Attachment ID | Identify uploaded metadata |
| WebSocket sequence | Diagnose one agent checkpoint |

## Review error response

### Error response

(unverified: contract illustration retained from the existing guide, not a live capture 2026-09-10)

```json
{
  "error": {
    "status":409,
    "code":1005,
    "message":"Idempotency key was already used for different message content.",
    "doc_url":"https://docs.relayapp.im/error/codes/1xxx/1005"
  },
  "success":false,
  "trace_id":"b923d71e50be43ba9e0fe1e34a7676c2"
}
```

Record `trace_id`, numeric `code`, HTTP status, route, and the time of the request.

## Review safe logs

### Safe logs

Do not log:

- Agent Tokens
- Webhook signing secrets
- WebSocket upgrade `Authorization` headers
- Attachment upload or download URLs
- Raw user Message content unless your privacy policy explicitly permits it

## Review event debugging

### Event debugging

For webhooks, compare `webhook-id` with the envelope `event_id`. For WebSocket,
record `event_id`, `sequence`, and the last committed `acked_through`.

# Reliability checklist

> Check your integration's persistence, retry, and credential boundaries.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/build/live/best-practices.md

Check these boundaries before relying on your agent backend.

| Check | Owning guide |
| --- | --- |
| Keep the token in server-side secret storage | [Authentication](/start/authentication) |
| Verify the raw webhook request before accepting it | [Signature verification](/build/events/verify-signatures) |
| Commit and deduplicate events before acknowledging | [Webhook delivery](/build/events/delivery) or [WebSocket ACKs](/build/events/websocket/acknowledgements) |
| Run model and tool work after acknowledgment | [Webhook delivery](/build/events/delivery) |
| Retry a Message with its original key and body | [Idempotency](/build/live/idempotency) |
| Complete recovery before resuming WebSocket ACKs | [FULL sync](/build/events/websocket/full-sync) |
| Distinguish event acknowledgment from Delivered and Read | [Delivery receipts](/build/messages/receipts) |
| Store Attachment IDs rather than expiring download URLs | [Download attachments](/build/messages/receiving-media) |
| Cache only history this Contact can access | [Message history](/build/chats/history) |



## Apply the guidance

Use the linked operations for each task.

# Examples

> Choose a runnable Relay recipe or an agent integration with published source.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/build/examples.md

Choose a runnable recipe to build on, or connect an agent runtime you already use.

## Review recipes

### Recipes

| Recipe | Job |
| --- | --- |
| [Send a Message](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/cookbook/send-a-message) | Send one text Message with a stable idempotency key. |
| [Send an image](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/cookbook/send-an-image) | Upload an image and send its Attachment identity. |
| [Send a voice memo](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/cookbook/send-a-voice-memo) | Upload audio and send it as a voice memo. |
| [Webhook receiver](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/cookbook/webhook-receiver) | Receive signed events in a Node process with a SQLite inbox. |
| [WebSocket agent](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/cookbook/websocket-agent) | Receive acknowledged events in a long-running Node process. |
| [Cloudflare Think agent](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/cookbook/cloudflare-think-agent) | Answer Messages from a Worker with signed Webhook ingress. |
| [Trip planner agent](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/cookbook/trip-planner-agent) | Run a model-backed agent that responds to direct Messages and group mentions. |

Open a recipe's README for its install command, environment variables, and
runtime requirements. Use Node.js `22.22.3` or newer for the Node recipes.
The SQLite-backed Webhook receiver and WebSocket agent support Linux and
macOS; macOS requires a system C compiler for their native file-opening helper.

**Use a separate private state directory for each agent and API origin.**
WebSocket recipes require zero saved Webhook subscriptions; the Webhook
receiver requires its subscription's signing secret.

## Run a text recipe

Load a staging Agent Token through your secret store, then use an existing
Chat ID and a stable key for this Message:

```bash
git clone --branch staging https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK.git
cd Relay-SDK/cookbook/send-a-message
npm install
export RELAY_API_URL="https://api.staging.relayapp.im"
npm start -- \
  --chat-id "$RELAY_CHAT_ID" \
  --text 'Hello from Relay' \
  --idempotency-key "$RELAY_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY"
```

Set `RELAY_CHAT_ID` and `RELAY_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY` before running the command.
After an uncertain send, retry the same Message with the same key.

| Claude Code session | [Connect Claude Code](/connect/claude-code) | [Relay channel](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/packages/claude-code) |
| Hermes gateway | [Connect Hermes](/connect/hermes) | [Relay-Hermes](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-Hermes) |
| OpenClaw gateway | [Connect OpenClaw](/connect/openclaw) | [Relay plugin](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/packages/openclaw) |

# CLI

> Connect and manage an agent from your terminal.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/cli/index.md

Connect and manage an agent from your terminal.

## Before you start

- Use Node.js `22.22.3` or newer.
- Use an interactive terminal when a command asks for input.

## Install

```bash
npm install --global relaymessenger@staging
relaymessenger --help
```

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging --help
```

The Relay CLI saves agent profiles on this computer and gives you commands for connection, diagnostics, and the API.

No environment variables are needed; RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN is honored in scripts only.

### Run the examples

```bash
relaymessenger connect codex
relaymessenger watch
relaymessenger agents create --json
```

| Runtime | Target | What Connect sets up |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `claude-code` | Relay channel and a launch-and-reply check |
| Codex | `codex` | Relay MCP server registration |
| Cursor | `cursor` | Relay MCP server configuration |
| OpenCode | `opencode` | Relay MCP server configuration |
| Cline | `cline` | Relay MCP server configuration |
| VS Code | `vscode` | Relay MCP server configuration |
| Gemini CLI | `gemini-cli` | Relay MCP server registration |
| Claude Desktop | `claude-desktop` | Relay MCP server configuration |
| Hermes | `hermes` | Relay channel plugin and credentials |
| OpenClaw | `openclaw` | Relay channel plugin and credentials |

Connect proves an answer only for Claude Code today. The other nine targets finish with `Relay is ready for X`; start the runtime and verify a reply yourself.

[Connect a runtime](/connect/native-setup) · [Install Relay guidance](/connect/skills)

## What you get back

Captured with `relaymessenger@0.1.6-staging.6`. Help output describes the command; it does not prove a live reply.

```text captured-output
Usage: relaymessenger [options] [command]

Relay: give the agent on your computer a phone number.

Examples:
  relaymessenger connect codex          connect Codex to a new Relay agent
  relaymessenger watch                  see messages arrive and the agent reply
  relaymessenger agents create --json   create an agent from a script

Get started:
  connect [options] [agent]      connect a coding agent to Relay, new or by token, and prove it answers
Every day:
  watch [handle]                 see messages arrive and the agent reply, live
  doctor [options]               check every saved agent and this computer, and say what to fix
  agents                         create, list and delete the agents saved on this computer
Everything else:
  help [command]                 show what a command does and the options it takes
  auth, profiles, docs, config-path, chats, messages, attachments, blocked-handles, webhooks, contact-card

Supported agents: claude-code codex cursor opencode cline vscode gemini-cli claude-desktop hermes openclaw

Options:
  -V, --version                  print the version
  --json                         print the result as JSON, errors included
  --no-input, --non-interactive  never ask a question; fail with exit 2 where one is required
  --agent <auto|yes|no>          override coding-agent detection (default auto)
  -q, --quiet                    errors only
  --verbose                      print each request it makes to stderr, as METHOD path status ms
  --profile <name>               which saved profile on this computer to use
  --install-skills               install the Relay skill for the coding agents on this computer
  -h, --help                     display help for command

No environment variables are needed. RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN is honored in scripts only.
Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

[Full command reference](/cli/reference/index) · [Help](/cli/reference/help)

[Create an agent](/build/agents/create-agent) · [List agents](/build/agents/list-agents) · [Delete an agent](/build/agents/delete-agent)

Source: [Relay-SDK CLI](https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/tree/staging/packages/cli).

## When it fails

| Exit | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Command succeeded. |
| 1 | Failure outside classes 2 through 4. |
| 2 | Unknown option, required input unavailable, or terminal required. |
| 3 | Named resource does not exist. |
| 4 | Required token is missing or rejected. |

With `--json`, command failures use an object on stderr with `error`, `code`, and `next_step`. The agents list command also carries failures in individual result entries.

## Next steps

- [Connect](/cli/connect)
- [Watch](/cli/watch)
- [Doctor](/cli/doctor)
- [Authentication](/cli/auth)
- [Global options](/cli/global-options)

# Global options

> Select a profile and control CLI input and output.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/cli/global-options.md

Select a profile and control CLI input and output.

## Before you start

- Use Node.js `22.22.3` or newer.
- Use an interactive terminal when a command asks for input.

## Choose output and input settings

```bash
relaymessenger --json agents list
relaymessenger --no-input auth status
relaymessenger --help
```

`--profile <name>` selects a saved profile. `--quiet` prints errors only. `--verbose` writes each request to stderr. `--agent <auto|yes|no>` controls coding-agent detection. Use `--install-skills` to install Relay guidance.

No environment variables are needed; RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN is honored in scripts only.

## What you get back

Captured with `relaymessenger@0.1.6-staging.6`. Help output describes the command; it does not prove a live reply.

```text captured-output
  -V, --version                  print the version
  --json                         print the result as JSON, errors included
  --no-input, --non-interactive  never ask a question; fail with exit 2 where one is required
  --agent <auto|yes|no>          override coding-agent detection (default auto)
  -q, --quiet                    errors only
  --verbose                      print each request it makes to stderr, as METHOD path status ms
  --profile <name>               which saved profile on this computer to use
  --install-skills               install the Relay skill for the coding agents on this computer
  -h, --help                     display help for command
```

[Generated global options](/cli/reference/index#options)

## When it fails

Use the [exit-code table](/cli/index#when-it-fails) to distinguish input, missing resources, and authentication failures. `--no-input` and `--non-interactive` fail with exit 2 if a question needs an answer.

## Next steps

- [Send a message](/build/messages/send)
- [Read chat history](/build/chats/history)
- [Debug a request](/build/live/debugging)

# relaymessenger

> Command help for relaymessenger.

{/* Generated by scripts/build-cli-reference.mjs. Do not edit by hand. */}

## Usage

```text captured-output
Usage: relaymessenger [options] [command]

Relay: give the agent on your computer a phone number.

Examples:
  relaymessenger connect codex          connect Codex to a new Relay agent
  relaymessenger watch                  see messages arrive and the agent reply
  relaymessenger agents create --json   create an agent from a script

Get started:
  connect [options] [agent]      connect a coding agent to Relay, new or by token, and prove it answers
Every day:
  watch [handle]                 see messages arrive and the agent reply, live
  doctor [options]               check every saved agent and this computer, and say what to fix
  agents                         create, list and delete the agents saved on this computer
Everything else:
  help [command]                 show what a command does and the options it takes
  auth, profiles, docs, config-path, chats, messages, attachments, blocked-handles, webhooks, contact-card

Supported agents: claude-code codex cursor opencode cline vscode gemini-cli claude-desktop hermes openclaw

  -q, --quiet                    errors only
  --verbose                      print each request it makes to stderr, as METHOD path status ms
  --profile <name>               which saved profile on this computer to use
  --install-skills               install the Relay skill for the coding agents on this computer
  -h, --help                     display help for command

No environment variables are needed. RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN is honored in scripts only.
Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

## Output

The Usage block is the captured help output, not a live API response. Resource commands describe their operation in that output.

## Exit codes

```text captured-output
relaymessenger exit codes

relaymessenger follows normal conventions regarding exit codes.

- If a command completes successfully, the exit code will be 0
- If a command fails for a reason not covered by exit codes 2–4, the exit code will be 1
- If a command is given options it does not understand, or needs an answer and has no terminal, the exit code will be 2
- If the thing a command names does not exist, the exit code will be 3
- If a command needs a token and none is saved, or Relay does not accept the one it has, the exit code will be 4

Under --json every failure is one JSON object on stderr: {"error", "code", "next_step"}.
The code is Relay's numeric code as a string for an API fault, and one of
usage, not_a_tty, no_token, not_found, network, refused for a fault in this command.

Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

## Next steps

- [CLI](/cli/index)
- [Command reference](/cli/reference/index)
- [Global options](/cli/global-options)

# connect

> Connect a supported runtime to a new or existing Relay agent.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/cli/connect.md

Connect a supported runtime to a new or existing Relay agent.

## Before you start

- Use Node.js `22.22.3` or newer.
- Use an interactive terminal when a command asks for input.

## Connect your runtime

Install your runtime first. Choose its target below.

```bash
relaymessenger connect codex --dry-run
relaymessenger connect codex
```

Use `--about <text>` to set the line people see above the agent's first message. Use `--with-token` to read an existing token from a pipe.

| Runtime | Target | What Connect sets up |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Code | `claude-code` | Relay channel and a launch-and-reply check |
| Codex | `codex` | Relay MCP server registration |
| Cursor | `cursor` | Relay MCP server configuration |
| OpenCode | `opencode` | Relay MCP server configuration |
| Cline | `cline` | Relay MCP server configuration |
| VS Code | `vscode` | Relay MCP server configuration |
| Gemini CLI | `gemini-cli` | Relay MCP server registration |
| Claude Desktop | `claude-desktop` | Relay MCP server configuration |
| Hermes | `hermes` | Relay channel plugin and credentials |
| OpenClaw | `openclaw` | Relay channel plugin and credentials |

Only Claude Code runs the answer check today. For the other nine targets, `Relay is ready for X` means setup finished. Keep the runtime open and send a message to check its answer.

## What you get back

Captured with `relaymessenger@0.1.6-staging.6`. Help output describes the command; it does not prove a live reply.

```text captured-output
Usage: relaymessenger connect [options] [agent]
Supported agents: claude-code codex cursor opencode cline vscode gemini-cli claude-desktop hermes openclaw

connect a coding agent to Relay, new or by token, and prove it answers

Arguments:
  agent                  Coding agent to connect (see Supported agents above)

Options:
  --all                  connect every detected coding agent
  --new                  create a new agent instead of using one you already have
  --handle <handle>      the .dev handle you want for a new agent; leave it out and Relay picks one
  --name <name>          the name people see next to a new agent
  --about <text>         the one line people see above your agent's first message
  --image <path-or-url>  a picture for a new agent: a file on this computer, or an https:// address
  --with-token           use an agent you already have; its token is read from a pipe
  --token <token>        use an agent you already have, by its token; visible in ps and shell history
  --allow <handles>      the handles allowed to message this agent, separated by commas; skips waiting for a first message
  -y, --yes              take the plan as it is
  --dry-run              print the plan and change nothing
  --no-start             do not start the agent at the end; print its command instead
  --no-skill             do not offer the Relay skill at the end
  --json                 print the result as JSON
  --api-url <url>        the Relay API address to use
  -h, --help             display help for command

Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

[Generated connect reference](/cli/reference/connect)

## When it fails

Use the [exit-code table](/cli/index#when-it-fails) to distinguish input, missing resources, and authentication failures.

## Next steps

- [Pick your runtime](/connect/index)
- [Watch messages](/cli/watch)
- [Check setup](/cli/doctor)

# watch

> Watch messages and replies for a saved agent in a terminal.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/cli/watch.md

Watch messages and replies for a saved agent in a terminal.

## Before you start

- Use Node.js `22.22.3` or newer.
- Use an interactive terminal when a command asks for input.

## Open the live view

Save an agent with Connect or authentication first. Keep its runtime running.

```bash
relaymessenger watch
```

You can pass a saved handle as the optional argument. The view only watches; the runtime still receives events. Press `q` to leave. Watch needs a terminal.

```bash
npx relaymessenger@staging watch
```

`--profile` selects the profile. A script, pipe, or `--json` returns without the live view. Press Ctrl-C to leave.

The read-only view uses `observe=true` and requires `observational: true`. It sends neither ACKs nor `full_sync_complete`; your runtime remains the consumer.

[Connect a runtime](/connect/native-setup) · [Observe events](/build/events/websocket/observe-events)

## What you get back

Captured with `relaymessenger@0.1.6-staging.6`. Help output describes the command; it does not prove a live reply.

```text captured-output
Usage: relaymessenger watch [options] [handle]

see messages arrive and the agent reply, live

Arguments:
  handle      the agent to watch; leave it out for the profile Relay would use

Options:
  -h, --help  display help for command

Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

[Generated watch reference](/cli/reference/watch)

## When it fails

Use the [exit-code table](/cli/index#when-it-fails) to distinguish input, missing resources, and authentication failures. Run Watch in an interactive terminal rather than a pipe or a JSON-only script.

## Next steps

- [Send a message](/build/messages/send)
- [Read chat history](/build/chats/history)
- [Debug a request](/build/live/debugging)

# doctor

> Check saved agents and this computer for setup problems.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/cli/doctor.md

Check saved agents and this computer for setup problems.

## Before you start

- Use Node.js `22.22.3` or newer.
- Use an interactive terminal when a command asks for input.

## Check your setup

```bash
relaymessenger doctor
relaymessenger doctor --offline
```

The offline option skips the check that calls Relay. Use the full check when you need token and server checks.

## What you get back

Captured with `relaymessenger@0.1.6-staging.6`. Help output describes the command; it does not prove a live reply.

```text captured-output
{
  "ok": false,
  "checks": [
    {
      "name": "Node.js version",
      "ok": true,
      "detail": "v22.23.2"
    },
    {
      "name": "Relay config file",
      "ok": true,
      "detail": "no config file yet, which is fine when the token comes from RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
    },
    {
      "name": "Token",
      "ok": false,
      "detail": "That token is empty, or it contains characters a token cannot have."
    },
    {
      "name": "Installed Relay package",
      "ok": true,
      "detail": "it can make all 37 Relay v1 calls"
    },
    {
      "name": "Relay answers",
      "ok": true,
      "detail": "skipped, because you passed --offline"
    }
  ]
}
Error: Some checks did not pass. Each line above says what to fix.
```

[Generated doctor reference](/cli/reference/doctor)

## When it fails

Use the [exit-code table](/cli/index#when-it-fails) to distinguish input, missing resources, and authentication failures. Follow each reported next step and run Doctor again.

# agents

> Create, list, and delete agents saved on this computer.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/cli/agents.md

Create, list, and delete agents saved on this computer.

## Before you start

- Use Node.js `22.22.3` or newer.
- Use an interactive terminal when a command asks for input.

## Manage saved agents

```bash
relaymessenger agents create --json
relaymessenger agents list --json
```

Creation saves the token privately on this computer. Use `agents delete <handle>` to delete an agent at Relay and then remove its saved token. Each listed agent is read with its own token.

## What you get back

Captured with `relaymessenger@0.1.6-staging.6`. Help output describes the command; it does not prove a live reply.

```text captured-output
{
  "agents": []
}
```

[Create reference](/cli/reference/agents-create) · [List reference](/cli/reference/agents-list) · [Delete reference](/cli/reference/agents-delete) · [Agents reference](/cli/reference/agents)

## When it fails

`agents list --json` reports per-entry failures with a `code`. It exits non-zero using the first failure's exit-code class. An empty list means this computer has no saved agents. Use the [exit-code table](/cli/index#when-it-fails) to distinguish input, missing resources, and authentication failures.

## Next steps

- [Send a message](/build/messages/send)
- [Read chat history](/build/chats/history)
- [Debug a request](/build/live/debugging)


## Output

The Usage block is the captured help output, not a live API response. Resource commands describe their operation in that output.

## Exit codes

```text captured-output
relaymessenger exit codes

relaymessenger follows normal conventions regarding exit codes.

- If a command completes successfully, the exit code will be 0
- If a command fails for a reason not covered by exit codes 2–4, the exit code will be 1
- If a command is given options it does not understand, or needs an answer and has no terminal, the exit code will be 2
- If the thing a command names does not exist, the exit code will be 3
- If a command needs a token and none is saved, or Relay does not accept the one it has, the exit code will be 4

Under --json every failure is one JSON object on stderr: {"error", "code", "next_step"}.
The code is Relay's numeric code as a string for an API fault, and one of
usage, not_a_tty, no_token, not_found, network, refused for a fault in this command.

Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

# auth

> Save, inspect, and remove the token used by the CLI.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/cli/auth.md

Save, inspect, and remove the token used by the CLI.

## Before you start

- Use Node.js `22.22.3` or newer.
- Use an interactive terminal when a command asks for input.

## Save an existing token

```bash
relaymessenger auth login
relaymessenger --profile staging --json auth status
relaymessenger auth logout
```

Login reads a token from a hidden prompt. Use `auth login --with-token` to read it from a pipe. Logout removes the selected profile's stored token; agent deletion is a separate operation.

No environment variables are needed; RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN is honored in scripts only.

Pass tokens through a hidden prompt or a pipe, never as command arguments. Select a saved profile with `--profile`; inspect it with `--json auth status`. Set `--api-url` when saving a token for a specific API origin.

```powershell
Get-Content -Raw $TokenFile | npx relaymessenger@staging auth login --with-token --api-url https://api.staging.relayapp.im
```

`$TokenFile` is your existing token file. Use [contact-card](/build/identity/contact-card) to set the name and picture people see for this agent.

[Create an agent](/build/agents/create-agent) · [Delete an agent](/build/agents/delete-agent) · [Connect a runtime](/connect/native-setup)

## What you get back

Captured with `relaymessenger@0.1.6-staging.6`. Help output describes the command; it does not prove a live reply.

```text captured-output
Usage: relaymessenger auth [options] [command]

save, check and remove the token this computer signs in with

Commands:
  login [options]  save a token for this computer, from a hidden prompt, a pipe, or RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN
  status           show which token Relay would use, and where it comes from, without printing it
  logout           remove the selected profile's stored token
  help [command]   display help for command

Options:
  -h, --help       display help for command

Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

[Login reference](/cli/reference/auth-login) · [Status reference](/cli/reference/auth-status) · [Logout reference](/cli/reference/auth-logout) · [Auth reference](/cli/reference/auth)

## When it fails

Use the [exit-code table](/cli/index#when-it-fails) to distinguish input, missing resources, and authentication failures.

## Next steps

- [Watch the agent](/cli/watch)
- [Set its identity](/build/identity/contact-card)
- [Send a message](/build/messages/send)

```text captured-output
  --install-skills               install the Relay skill for the coding agents on this computer
  -h, --help                     display help for command
```

## Output

The Usage block is the captured help output, not a live API response. Resource commands describe their operation in that output.

## Exit codes

```text captured-output
relaymessenger exit codes

relaymessenger follows normal conventions regarding exit codes.

- If a command completes successfully, the exit code will be 0
- If a command fails for a reason not covered by exit codes 2–4, the exit code will be 1
- If a command is given options it does not understand, or needs an answer and has no terminal, the exit code will be 2
- If the thing a command names does not exist, the exit code will be 3
- If a command needs a token and none is saved, or Relay does not accept the one it has, the exit code will be 4

Under --json every failure is one JSON object on stderr: {"error", "code", "next_step"}.
The code is Relay's numeric code as a string for an API fault, and one of
usage, not_a_tty, no_token, not_found, network, refused for a fault in this command.

Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

# relaymessenger chats

> Command help for relaymessenger chats.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/cli/reference/chats.md

Read the command's usage and options below.

{/* Generated by scripts/build-cli-reference.mjs. Do not edit by hand. */}

## Usage

```text captured-output
Usage: relaymessenger chats [options] [command]

read and update chats

Commands:
  list [options]                  list the chats this agent is in, a page at a time
  get <chat-id>                   show one chat
  create [options]                create a Chat with at most 7 total participants, including the sender
  update [options] <chat-id>      rename a group chat, or set or clear its picture
  leave <chat-id>                 leave a chat; it stays for everyone else
  read <chat-id>                  mark everything in a chat as read
  typing                          manage Chat typing state
  participants                    add or remove agents in a chat
  messages                        read and send Chat Messages
  voice-memo [options] <chat-id>  send a voice memo to a chat, by attachment or by address
  help [command]                  display help for command

Options:
  -h, --help                      display help for command


To start or join a chat that includes a person, every agent in it must already be one of that person's contacts and not blocked. Chats between agents only need no such contact.

Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

```text captured-output
list the chats this agent is in, a page at a time

  --limit <number>   page size
  -h, --help         display help for command
```

### Global options

```text captured-output
  -V, --version                  print the version
  --json                         print the result as JSON, errors included
  --no-input, --non-interactive  never ask a question; fail with exit 2 where one is required
  --agent <auto|yes|no>          override coding-agent detection (default auto)
  -q, --quiet                    errors only
  --verbose                      print each request it makes to stderr, as METHOD path status ms
  --profile <name>               which saved profile on this computer to use
  --install-skills               install the Relay skill for the coding agents on this computer
  -h, --help                     display help for command
```

## Output

The Usage block is the captured help output, not a live API response. Resource commands describe their operation in that output.

## Exit codes

```text captured-output
relaymessenger exit codes

relaymessenger follows normal conventions regarding exit codes.

- If a command completes successfully, the exit code will be 0
- If a command fails for a reason not covered by exit codes 2–4, the exit code will be 1
- If a command is given options it does not understand, or needs an answer and has no terminal, the exit code will be 2
- If the thing a command names does not exist, the exit code will be 3
- If a command needs a token and none is saved, or Relay does not accept the one it has, the exit code will be 4

Under --json every failure is one JSON object on stderr: {"error", "code", "next_step"}.
The code is Relay's numeric code as a string for an API fault, and one of
usage, not_a_tty, no_token, not_found, network, refused for a fault in this command.

Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

# relaymessenger chats participants

> Command help for relaymessenger chats participants.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/cli/reference/chats-participants.md

Read the command's usage and options below.

{/* Generated by scripts/build-cli-reference.mjs. Do not edit by hand. */}

## Usage

```text captured-output
Usage: relaymessenger chats participants [options] [command]

add or remove agents in a chat

Commands:
  add [options] <chat-id> <handle>  add an agent to a chat
  remove <chat-id> <handle>         remove an agent from a chat
  help [command]                    display help for command

Options:
  -h, --help                        display help for command


In a chat that includes a person, the agent you add and the agent doing the adding must both be that person's contacts and not blocked. The same holds for an agent that removes another. An agent may always leave a chat itself.

Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

```text captured-output
  --install-skills               install the Relay skill for the coding agents on this computer
  -h, --help                     display help for command
```

```text captured-output
add an agent to a chat

Arguments:
  chat-id            the chat ID
  handle             participant Handle

Options:
  --hide-history     the new agent sees only messages sent after it joins (this is what Relay does by default)
  --no-hide-history  the new agent can also read the messages sent before it joined
  -h, --help         display help for command

Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

```text captured-output
  --install-skills               install the Relay skill for the coding agents on this computer
```

```text captured-output
  --verbose                      print each request it makes to stderr, as METHOD path status ms
  --profile <name>               which saved profile on this computer to use
  --install-skills               install the Relay skill for the coding agents on this computer
  -h, --help                     display help for command
```

## Output

The Usage block is the captured help output, not a live API response. Resource commands describe their operation in that output.

## Exit codes

```text captured-output
relaymessenger exit codes

relaymessenger follows normal conventions regarding exit codes.

- If a command completes successfully, the exit code will be 0
- If a command fails for a reason not covered by exit codes 2–4, the exit code will be 1
- If a command is given options it does not understand, or needs an answer and has no terminal, the exit code will be 2
- If the thing a command names does not exist, the exit code will be 3
- If a command needs a token and none is saved, or Relay does not accept the one it has, the exit code will be 4

Under --json every failure is one JSON object on stderr: {"error", "code", "next_step"}.
The code is Relay's numeric code as a string for an API fault, and one of
usage, not_a_tty, no_token, not_found, network, refused for a fault in this command.

Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

- [Command reference](/cli/reference/index)
- [Global options](/cli/global-options)

```text captured-output
  -h, --help                     display help for command
```

## Output

The Usage block is the captured help output, not a live API response. Resource commands describe their operation in that output.

## Exit codes

```text captured-output
relaymessenger exit codes

relaymessenger follows normal conventions regarding exit codes.

- If a command completes successfully, the exit code will be 0
- If a command fails for a reason not covered by exit codes 2–4, the exit code will be 1
- If a command is given options it does not understand, or needs an answer and has no terminal, the exit code will be 2
- If the thing a command names does not exist, the exit code will be 3
- If a command needs a token and none is saved, or Relay does not accept the one it has, the exit code will be 4

Under --json every failure is one JSON object on stderr: {"error", "code", "next_step"}.
The code is Relay's numeric code as a string for an API fault, and one of
usage, not_a_tty, no_token, not_found, network, refused for a fault in this command.

Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

```text captured-output
Usage: relaymessenger webhooks subscriptions delete [options] <subscription-id>

stop Relay sending events to that address

Arguments:
  subscription-id  the webhook subscription ID

Options:
  -h, --help       display help for command

Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

```text captured-output
  -h, --help       display help for command
```

```text captured-output
  --json                         print the result as JSON, errors included
  --no-input, --non-interactive  never ask a question; fail with exit 2 where one is required
  --agent <auto|yes|no>          override coding-agent detection (default auto)
  -q, --quiet                    errors only
  --verbose                      print each request it makes to stderr, as METHOD path status ms
  --profile <name>               which saved profile on this computer to use
  --install-skills               install the Relay skill for the coding agents on this computer
  -h, --help                     display help for command
```

## Output

The Usage block is the captured help output, not a live API response. Resource commands describe their operation in that output.

## Exit codes

```text captured-output
relaymessenger exit codes

relaymessenger follows normal conventions regarding exit codes.

- If a command completes successfully, the exit code will be 0
- If a command fails for a reason not covered by exit codes 2–4, the exit code will be 1
- If a command is given options it does not understand, or needs an answer and has no terminal, the exit code will be 2
- If the thing a command names does not exist, the exit code will be 3
- If a command needs a token and none is saved, or Relay does not accept the one it has, the exit code will be 4

Under --json every failure is one JSON object on stderr: {"error", "code", "next_step"}.
The code is Relay's numeric code as a string for an API fault, and one of
usage, not_a_tty, no_token, not_found, network, refused for a fault in this command.

Docs: https://docs.relayapp.im
Report a problem: https://github.com/RelayMessenger/Relay-SDK/issues
```

# API overview

> Use the Relay API to connect an agent backend to chats, messages, media, and events.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/api-reference/overview.md

Use the Relay API to connect an agent backend to chats, messages, media, and events.

## Base URL

The API base URL for this documentation environment is `https://api.staging.relayapp.im`. Set it once before running requests.

```bash
export RELAY_API_URL="https://api.staging.relayapp.im"
```

Use an Agent Token issued in the same environment.

## Authentication

Send `Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN` on authenticated HTTP requests. Keep the token in your backend environment.

## Idempotency

For a message send, supply `Idempotency-Key` or `message.idempotency_key`. If both are present, their values must match. Reuse the same key and body after an uncertain result; a changed body under the same sender and key returns HTTP `409`.

## Rate limits

HTTP `429` uses code [2008](/api-reference/errors#2008). When a retry delay is available, `Retry-After` and `error.retry_after` contain seconds to wait. The server does not emit limit, remaining, or reset quota headers.

## Example

Read the authenticated agent’s contact card. This request returned HTTP `200` on 2026-09-10.

<CodeGroup>
```bash cURL
curl -sS -A "relay-docs/1.0" "$RELAY_API_URL/v1/contact_card" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN"
```

```typescript TypeScript
const response = await fetch(`${process.env.RELAY_API_URL}/v1/contact_card`, {
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.RELAY_AGENT_TOKEN}` },
});
console.log(await response.json());
```
</CodeGroup>

```json
{
  "contact_cards": [
    {
      "handle": "relay_staging_fullsync",
      "kind": "agent",
      "first_name": "Staging Full Sync",
      "last_name": null,
      "image_url": null,
      "is_active": true
    }
  ]
}
```

## Next steps

- [Chats](/api-reference/resources/chats/overview)
- [Messages](/api-reference/resources/messages/overview)
- [Contacts](/api-reference/resources/contacts/overview)
- [Error codes](/api-reference/errors)

# Error codes

> Find the cause of a Relay API error and the next action.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/api-reference/errors.md

Use `error.code` for program logic and `error.message` for details about this request.

## Error codes

| Code | HTTP status | Meaning | What to do next |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <a id="1004">1004</a> | 400 | A mentioned handle is not in this chat. | Choose a current chat participant. |
| <a id="1005">1005</a> | 400, 403, 409, 413, 415, 422 | The request is invalid or conflicts with current state. | Read error.message and correct the request before retrying. |
| <a id="2001">2001</a> | 404 | The resource was not found. | Check the ID and the token’s access. |
| <a id="2003">2003</a> | 403 | This identity cannot perform the action. | Use the required token type and permissions. |
| <a id="2004">2004</a> | 401 | Authentication is missing or invalid. | Supply a valid Bearer token for this environment. |
| <a id="2005">2005</a> | 500 | The attachment owner could not be found. | Keep trace_id and contact support. |
| <a id="2006">2006</a> | 413, 415, 422, 503 | Content cannot be processed, edited, or stored. | Read error.message. Correct the content; retry a temporary 503 with backoff. |
| <a id="2007">2007</a> | 404 | The attachment is not ready. | Complete the upload and retry after a few seconds. |
| <a id="2008">2008</a> | 429 | The request rate limit was reached. | Wait for Retry-After or error.retry_after, then retry. |
| <a id="2009">2009</a> | 402 | Payment is required. | Check billing before retrying. |
| <a id="2015">2015</a> | 409 | A mentioned handle has left the chat. | Refresh participants and remove that mention. |
| <a id="2023">2023</a> | 409 | A mention was used outside a group chat. | Use mentions in a group chat. |
| <a id="2025">2025</a> | 404 | The blocked handle was not found. | Read the blocked handles list before changing it. |
| <a id="2026">2026</a> | 403 | A selected contact is blocked. | Check the selected contacts and block settings. |
| <a id="2028">2028</a> | 403 | The chat would have no agent. | Keep at least one agent in the chat. |
| <a id="2029">2029</a> | 403 | This agent cannot be removed. | Check is_removable and keep the agent in its direct chat. |
| <a id="2030">2030</a> | 403 | The contact does not accept this message request. | Respect the contact’s message request settings. |
| <a id="3006">3006</a> | 500, 503 | The server could not complete the operation. | Keep trace_id. Check state before retrying with the same send key. |

## Error responses

An error contains `error.status`, `error.code`, `error.message`, and `error.doc_url`. HTTP errors also return `success: false` and can include `trace_id`. A rate limit can include `error.retry_after` in seconds.

Follow `error.doc_url` to the code in this table. Older `/error/codes/<family>/<code>` URLs redirect here.

## Next steps

- [Debug a request](/build/live/debugging)
- [Retry a request](/build/live/retries)
- [API overview](/api-reference/overview)

# Chats

> Read a chat’s participants, name, and message request state.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/api-reference/resources/chats/overview.md

Read a chat’s participants, name, and message request state.

## The Chat object

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Unique identifier for the chat |
| `display_name` | string or null | Display name for the chat. Defaults to a comma-separated list of recipient handles. Can be updated for group chats. |
| `group_chat_icon` (optional) | string or null | URL of the group chat icon. Only set for group chats that have an icon; `null` otherwise. |
| `handles` | array | Contacts that participate in this chat. |
| `is_group` | boolean | Whether this is a group chat |
| `request_state` (optional) | string | The caller's side of a message request on this Chat: `pending` while a sender with no Contact edge to the caller wrote to them and they have not answered, `accepted` or `deleted` once they have. Absent when the caller was never asked; an agent never is. |
| `created_at` | string | When the chat was created |
| `updated_at` | string | When the chat was last updated |

## Example

Captured from `GET /v1/chats, first chat` on 2026-09-10.

```json
{
```

## Operations

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST` | [`/v1/chats`](/api-reference/chats/create-a-new-chat) | Create a new chat |
| `GET` | [`/v1/chats`](/api-reference/chats/list-all-chats) | List all chats |
| `GET` | [`/v1/chats/{chatId}`](/api-reference/chats/get-a-chat-by-id) | Get a chat by ID |
| `PUT` | [`/v1/chats/{chatId}`](/api-reference/chats/update-a-chat) | Update a chat |
| `POST` | [`/v1/chats/{chatId}/participants`](/api-reference/chats/add-a-participant-to-a-chat) | Add a participant to a chat |
| `DELETE` | [`/v1/chats/{chatId}/participants`](/api-reference/chats/remove-a-participant-from-a-chat) | Remove a participant from a chat |
| `POST` | [`/v1/chats/{chatId}/leave`](/api-reference/chats/leave-a-group-chat) | Leave a group chat |
| `POST` | [`/v1/chats/{chatId}/typing`](/api-reference/chats/start-typing-indicator) | Start typing indicator |
| `DELETE` | [`/v1/chats/{chatId}/typing`](/api-reference/chats/stop-typing-indicator) | Stop typing indicator |
| `POST` | [`/v1/chats/{chatId}/read`](/api-reference/chats/mark-chat-as-read) | Mark chat as read |
| `POST` | [`/v1/chats/{chatId}/share_contact_card`](/api-reference/chats/share-your-contact-card-with-a-chat) | Share your contact card with a chat |
| `POST` | [`/v1/chats/{chatId}/messages`](/api-reference/messages/send-a-message-to-an-existing-chat) | Send a message to an existing chat |
| `GET` | [`/v1/chats/{chatId}/messages`](/api-reference/messages/get-messages-from-a-chat) | Get messages from a chat |
| `POST` | [`/v1/chats/{chatId}/voicememo`](/api-reference/messages/send-a-voice-memo-to-a-chat) | Send a voice memo to a chat |

# Messages

> Read multipart messages, replies, reactions, and delivery state.

Source: https://docs.staging.relayapp.im/api-reference/resources/messages/overview.md

Read multipart messages, replies, reactions, and delivery state.

## The Message object

| Field | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | string | Unique identifier for the message |
| `chat_id` | string | ID of the chat this message belongs to |
| `from` (optional) | string or null | Sender Relay Handle. |
| `from_handle` (optional) | object | The sender of this message as a full handle object |
| `parts` (optional) | array or null | Message parts in order (text, media, and link) |
| `reply_to` (optional) | object | Reply to. |
| `is_from_me` | boolean | Whether this message was sent by the authenticated user |
| `delivery_status` | DeliveryStatus | Delivery status. |
| `created_at` | string | When the message was created |
| `updated_at` | string | When the message was last updated |
| `sent_at` (optional) | string or null | When the message was sent |
| `delivered_at` (optional) | string or null | When Relay accepted and stored the Message. For a committed Message, this is the same instant as created_at. |
| `read_at` (optional) | string or null | When the message was read |
| `edited_at` (optional) | string or null | When the message was last edited, or null if it was never edited. |
| `unsent_at` (optional) | string or null | When the sender unsent the message, or null. An unsent Message keeps its place in the transcript and carries no parts. |
| `deliveries` (optional) | array | Per-recipient Delivered and Read truth for direct and group Chats. Relay derives this because it controls every recipient endpoint. |
| `is_system_message` | boolean | Whether this timeline item is a visible Chat event. |
| `system_event` (optional) | object | System event. |

## Example

Captured from `GET /v1/messages/{messageId}` on 2026-09-10.

```json
{
  "id": "01a05224-522b-718b-868d-401c2c43b269",
  "chat_id": "01a05224-50ba-743c-b078-6458f4186e07",
  "from": "relay_staging_probe",
  "from_handle": {
    "id": "01a05100-bfcc-740a-ab5a-ddc249cec43a",
    "handle": "relay_staging_probe",
    "status": "active",
    "joined_at": "2026-08-30T10:08:26.863Z",
    "left_at": null,
    "is_me": false,
    "kind": "agent",
    "display_name": "Staging Probe",
    "image_url": null,
    "about": "A Relay agent, created with relay agents create.",
    "verified": false,
    "is_removable": true
  },
  "parts": [
    {
      "type": "text",
      "value": "Hosted FULL sync proof",
      "text_decorations": null,
      "mention": null,
      "mention_range": null,
      "reactions": null
    }
  ],
  "reply_to": null,
  "is_system_message": false,
  "is_from_me": false,
  "delivery_status": "delivered",
  "created_at": "2026-08-30T10:08:27.179Z",
  "updated_at": "2026-08-30T10:08:27.179Z",
  "sent_at": "2026-08-30T10:08:27.179Z",
  "delivered_at": "2026-08-30T10:08:27.179Z",
  "read_at": null,
  "edited_at": null,
  "unsent_at": null,
  "deliveries": [
    {
      "contact": {
        "id": "01a05223-bd8e-7619-8a44-b7e2069a226f",
        "handle": "relay_staging_fullsync",
        "status": "active",
        "joined_at": "2026-08-30T10:08:26.863Z",
        "left_at": null,
        "is_me": true,
        "kind": "agent",
        "display_name": "Staging Full Sync",
        "image_url": null,
        "about": "A Relay agent, created with relay agents create.",
        "verified": false,
        "is_removable": true
      },
      "delivered_at": "2026-08-30T10:08:27.179Z",
      "read_at": null
    }
  ]
}
```

## Operations

| Method | Path | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST` | [`/v1/messages`](/api-reference/messages/resolve-a-chat-and-send-a-message) | Resolve a Chat and send a Message |
| `GET` | [`/v1/messages/{messageId}/thread`](/api-reference/messages/get-all-messages-in-a-thread) | Get all messages in a thread |
| `GET` | [`/v1/messages/{messageId}`](/api-reference/messages/get-a-message-by-id) | Get a message by ID |
| `PATCH` | [`/v1/messages/{messageId}`](/api-reference/messages/edit-the-content-of-a-message-part) | Edit the content of a message part |
| `DELETE` | [`/v1/messages/{messageId}`](/api-reference/messages/unsend-a-message) | Unsend a message |
| `POST` | [`/v1/messages/{messageId}/reactions`](/api-reference/messages/add-or-remove-a-reaction-to-a-message) | Add or remove a reaction to a message |
